colleagues and my dearest students, I take great pleasure that this 62 nd Convocation is being graced by none other than our National Security Advisor, Shri Ajit Doval . I am sure the graduands here are lucky to have Shri Doval as the Chief Guest today. Shri Ajit Doval has dedicated his life in the service of the nation right from his joining the Indian Police Service (IPS) almost six decades ago. I am sure, sir, your presence here will see many more entering the Services and dedicating their efforts to the development of our country. Thank you very much for accepting our invitation, sir. I am happy to welcome the world-renowned Dr. Padma Subrahmanyam, the recipient of all three Padma awards, and thank her for readily agreeing to grace this momentous occasion. I am sure it is apt to have her, an embodiment of dedication and devotion to Bharatnatyam (an Indian classical dance form), especially in the year when Fine Arts and Culture Excellence admissions are being introduced in our undergraduate admissions. Thank you, madam, I am sure your presence will inspire students to pursue their interests. IIT Madras (IITM) has had an eventful year with many major milestones, the top three being: achieving the Startup Shatham target; introducing admissions based on Fine Arts and Culture Excellence and Science Olympiad Excellence; and our performance in various university rankings. I am extremely happy that, surpassing the vision of Startup Shatham, the IIT Madras Incubation Cell (IITMIC) has incubated as many as 103 new deep core tech startups during 2024. This is our humble contribution to a Product Nation, a Startup Nation and Viksit Bharat 2047. Thanks to the collaborative efforts of IITMIC, with its sector- specific incubators like Pravartak, Bioincubator, Healthcare Technology Innovation Centre (HTIC) MedTech, the Rural Technology and Business Incubator (RTBI), and the School of Innovation and Entrepreneurship at IITM. 50% of these startups were founded by IIT Madras faculty, staff, students and alumni, and the remaining were founded by external entrepreneurs, showcasing the IITMIC's diverse entrepreneurial ecosystem. IIT Madras has become the first IIT in the country to introduce Fine Arts and Culture Excellence (FACE) admissions to undergraduate programmes from the academic year 2025-26. The objective of FACE admissions is to reward and encourage students who have achieved excellence in fine arts and culture. Two seats, a female-only seat and a gender-neutral seat, per programme will be allotted for FACE admissions to 1. all BTech and BS programmes of IIT Madras. In the current academic year, IIT Madras has also launched Science Olympiad Excellence (ScOpE) admissions to undergraduate programmes for students who excel in the National and International Olympiads. This admission is outside the Joint Entrance Examination (JEE) (Advanced) framework and has two supernumerary seats per programme, of which one seat will be exclusively for female students. Nearly six candidates offered FACE admissions have accepted the offers, and nearly twelve ScOpE offers have been made to eligible candidates. IIT Madras has proved herself by sustaining the top ranks in the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) : She has retained the #1 position for the sixth year in a row for overall performance among all universities in India and the #1 position among Engineering Institutes for the ninth year since inception of NIRF, and has ranked #2 in the Research Institutions and Innovation categories. IIT Madras has jumped 47 positions from the 227th rank last year to the 180th -position in the QS World University Rankings 2026 , becoming the 3rd in the country to be ranked below 200. IIT Madras has also won the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) Industrial Intellectual Property Awards 2024 in the category of academic institution for having the Best Patent Portfolio during the period 2019-24. IIT Madras was honoured with the prestigious 'CNBC-TV18 India Business Leader Award' (IBLA) for its unparalleled contribution to the Indian economy. IIT Madras also won the CII Award on Excellence for Women in STEM 2024. Thanks to the persistent efforts of the students, faculty, staff, alumni and industry partners without whose efforts this feat would not have been achievable. At this convocation, around 3227 graduands will receive their degrees. I am extremely happy that for the first time we will be awarding more than 500 PhD degrees. 529 students will receive PhD degrees, of whom 27 are external scholars from industry, and 250 will receive MS degrees of whom two are from industry and three from our IIT Madras Research Park. This year, 13 PhD scholars will receive joint degrees with foreign universities-one each with Nanyang University, Singapore; Tribhuvan University, Kathmandu, Nepal; National Tsing Hua University, Taiwan; Michigan State University, United States of America (USA); and the University of Toulouse, France; and two each with the Swinburne University of Technology, Australia; Rheinisch-Westfälische Technische Hochschule (RWTH) Aachen University, Germany; the University of Passau, Germany; and Curtin University, Australia.

heading: 1.1. Degree and Outreach Programmes
plain_text: ## 1.1. Degree and Outreach Programmes IIT Madras has undertaken many initiatives that are in congruence with the National Education Policy (NEP). The Institute Curriculum Task Force (CTF) has also made recommendations in consonance with the NEP, and has provided students with greater academic freedom in line with international programmes of a similar nature. The online BS in Data Science and Programming and the BS in Electronic Systems have been seeing increasing enrolments. It is heartening to learn that more than 38,000 students are pursuing the programmes, with nearly half of them pursuing them in parallel with another undergraduate programme. The programme also has some foreign students enrolled. The convocation and certificate distribution ceremony for these BS degree programmes was held early last month. I am very happy to record that three of our BS Data Science and Programming students have secured allIndia ranks (AIR) 1, 7 and 10 in the Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE) 2025. The Centre for Outreach and Digital Education (CODE) of IIT Madras has launched a few programmes this year. Partnering with the CII Institute of Logistics, CODE relaunched the highly successful (with around 40,000 trained in the past decade) Supply Chain Management Professional (SCMPro) certification programme, with a curriculum that provides participants with advanced skills to excel in the current dynamic and competitive industry landscape. Another first-of-its-kind Postgraduate Diploma programme in Process Safety seeks to enhance employees' capabilities in managing process safety challenges and reduce accidents in manufacturing, mining, energy and related sectors. Our Web-enabled MTech programmes enable industry personnel to upgrade their technical knowledge and skills at their own pace. More than 80 companies across diverse sectors have collaborated with the Centre to nominate their employees for this upskilling master's programme. A programme in E-mobility was the latest one launched in 2024. The programmes have so far benefitted more than 1200 industry personnel. In alignment with its Strategic Plan, IIT Madras is deepening its focus on the theme of local relevance leading to global excellence, as part of its broader vision of IITM for AllAnaivarukkum IITM. As part of this vision, initiatives such as Vidya Shakti and Kalvi Shakti are being actively pursued through the IIT Madras Pravartak Technologies Foundation, a Section 8 company established by the Institute. The underlying goal of Vidya Shakti is to facilitate a 50% gross enrolment ratio in colleges by 2035 by inspiring students towards education. Vidya Shakti-which started in October 2021 with providing live online classes in science, maths and English to rural students (of classes V to XII) in five villages-today reaches about 10 lakh students through its 7105 rural interaction centres that operate in seven Indian states (Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and Arunachal Pradesh) and also in Sri Lanka. Vidya Shakti has been recognised by the Hon'ble Education Minister Shri Dharmendra Pradhan, has been chosen as a disruptive and scalable model in education, and was endorsed by the Hon'ble Prime Minister of India during the Rising Bharat event held in Delhi in April 2025. Vidya Shakti relentlessly works towards capacity building, enabling teachers to embrace technology, get consistent attendance, and achieve improved outcomes. Technology intervention using simulation and gamification tools, teaching in students' mother tongues, and activity-based content are at the core of Vidya Shakti's pedagogy. We have trained 7500 teachers in simulation and gamification tools. We see a noticeable improvement in students based on our continuous micro-assessments, which are conducted every week. While the number of students securing lower marks has reduced, the number of students scoring higher marks in our multiple-choice question (MCQ) tests (both in TN and in UP) has increased. Students' attendance rates in our classes have also increased, as students are increasingly curious to learn concepts through activity-based learning content. Vidya Shakti aims at reaching 1 crore students in the academic year 2025-26. Through Pravartak Technologies, IITM leads two other programmes: Out of the Box Thinking and Sony Finishing School. Out of the Box Thinking (OOBT) is a national-level effort aimed at strengthening foundational mathematics and nurturing analytical thinking skills among learners of all ages. Delivered in multiple languages and accessible online, OOBT is designed to challenge conventional approaches and foster creative problem-solving from a young age. Another significant initiative is the Sony Finishing School, developed in collaboration with Sony India, which bridges the gap between academia and industry by equipping students with practical, domain-specific skills and soft skills training that enhances their employability, particularly in emerging technology sectors. IIT Madras has recently started an initiative called the IIT Madras School Connect programme to partner with schools to offer 8-week certification programmes that provide handson career experiences through introductory courses for Class X, XI, and XII students. This initiative was launched in 2024 with courses on data science and electronic systems. These courses were offered for four batches, and more than 50,000 students from 2400+ schools participated. We have now added certification courses on architecture, biological engineering, mathematics, computing, aerospace, ecology, humanities, and law. Through these programmes, we introduce cuttingedge technologies and provide hands-on training. Schools are invited to partner with us so that their students can benefit from these courses. As part of our ongoing commitment to science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) education, we have distributed electronic kits to 252 government schools across Tamil Nadu, enabling students from Classes IX to XII to perform electronics experiments. This initiative has already benefited nearly 22,000 students. With the integration of this programme into regular class hours in these schools from this academic year, the programme is expected to benefit over 1 lakh students. I would like to thank our alumni, without whose magnanimous donation this would not have been possible. The programme also has some foreign students enrolled. The convocation and certificate distribution ceremony for these BS degree programmes was held early last month. Another first-of-its-kind Postgraduate Diploma programme in Process Safety seeks to enhance employees' capabilities in managing process safety challenges and reduce accidents in manufacturing, mining, energy and related sectors. ## 1.2. Academic Research IIT Madras conducts cutting-edge research in emerging and disruptive technologies aimed at creating a lasting global impact. In the year under review, 42 high quality faculty have joined the Institute in carrying forward this cutting-edge research.

heading: 1.2.1. Snapshots of Research and Innovations
plain_text: ## 1.2.1. Snapshots of Research and Innovations IIT Madras has consistently strengthened initiatives to ensure that research conducted within her laboratories is effectively translated into technologies with meaningful societal impact. A few key highlights of these efforts are outlined below: IIT Madras has become the first research organization in the world to release the most detailed 3D high-resolution images of the foetal brain. For the first time globally, 5132 brain sections have been captured digitally using cuttingedge brain mapping technology developed by the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre in the Institute. This work will advance the field of neuroscience and potentially lead to the development of treatments for health conditions affecting the brain. IIT Madras launched the AMOLED Research Centre (ARC) to develop the next generation of active-matrix organic light-emitting diode (AMOLED) displays for smartphones, tablets, watches and wearables. It is funded by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India; Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO); and Tata Sons. This Centre will thus support the nation's initiative of developing a display manufacturing industry. The Extraterrestrial Manufacturing (ExTeM) Research Centre at IIT Madras has been at the forefront of India's space research. It is coming up with innovative processes to tackle the challenges of constructing infrastructure, 3D printing tools, and extracting materials crucial for sustainable space exploration. Our Hon'ble Prime Minister of India has mentioned the ExTeM in his Mann Ki Baat address on January 19, 2025. Researchers at the TTK Center for Rehabilitation Research and Device Development (R2D2), in collaboration with CMC Vellore, have developed PLUTO (Plug and Train Robot), a cost-effective and portable robot for hand rehabilitation. This patented technology offers precise therapeutic movements and real-time feedback, ensuring better outcomes for patients with conditions such as stroke, spinal cord injury, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease and post hand-surgery, among others. Researchers from the Centre of Excellence in Sports Science and Analytics (CESSA) have developed an indigenous portable Point-of-Care-Ultrasound Scanner (POCUS) for sports injury diagnosis and management. This research enables onfield diagnosis of injuries and immediate assessment of the extent of injury. Shri Jyotiraditya M Scindia, Hon'ble Minister of Communications and Minister of Development of North Eastern Region, Government of India, visited the fi rst-of-itskind indigenous 5G Testbed and witnessed a demonstration of the indigenous 5G network in the campus. Researchers at the 5G Testbed are currently working on designing and developing 6G technologies in addition to participating in global standardisation activities and developing Indian intellectual property rights (IPRs) in this critical sector. Under the National Quantum Mission of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, the IITM CDoT Samgnya Technologies Foundation (CDoT: Centre for Development of Telematics), a Section 8 company, has been set up at IIT Madras. This Quantum Communication Thematic Hub (T-hub) will focus on establishing India's quantum-secure communication network, deploying quantum key distribution (QKD) infrastructure, and guiding the nation's transition to post-quantum cryptography. The Foundation, in collaboration with industry and academia, aims to develop indigenous quantum solutions and position India as a global leader in secure next-generation technology. Dr. Aravind Kumar Chandiran's research group is working on solar energy storage and has made 20 significant advancements in the area of green hydrogen in the last year. One of the key achievements is the development of a >250 kW hydrogen microgrid in collaboration with Yokogawa Technology India Pvt Ltd. This microgrid mimics the future of renewable energy grids in India and has been established to study and understand energy management among different energy storage systems, to ensure 24×7 energy security. Dr. Chandiran, along with Dr. Raghuram Chetty (Chemical Engineering), Dr. Krishna Vasudevan (Electrical Engg.) and Dr. Muruganandam (Aerospace Engg.) established the Hyundai HTWO Hydrogen Innovation Centre at the IITM Discovery Campus that focuses on carrying out industrial R&D relevant to hydrogen space and enable faster adoption of hydrogen in power and mobility sectors. An Indian Army-IITM Research Centre, a dedicated Centre of Excellence, is being established to harness the potential of the Institute in various technology domains and serve as the nodal point for defence technology development projects and skilling of the personnel of the armed forces. The Centre will enable translational research and develop disruptive technologies for our armed forces indigenously. Dr. Prabhu Rajagopal's research group at the Automation & Data Engineering vertical of the Center for Nondestructive Evaluation (CNDE) focused on improved diagnostics through metamaterial-enhanced sensors, robotics, AI, quantum and distributed ledger technologies. Last year, Dr. Prabhu's group demonstrated bulk ultrasonic imaging down to an extraordinary resolution of 50 micrometres using micro-structured metalenses. His group is developing the Shobot suite of AI-enabled human collaborative robots for applications ranging from manufacturing and shopping assistance to geriatric homecare. Dr. Prabhu has published one of the first implementations of quantum machine learning for practical ultrasonic material diagnostics. His work on blockchain-based secure management of medical records has also gained wide appreciation. The Centre of Excellence (CoE) on NDE 5.0 (nondestructive evaluation) has launched the pioneering National Consortium for NDE (NCNDE) to promote translational research and product development for sensing and diagnostics; several multinational corporations (MNCs) and national industry majors such as Chevron, Waygate, Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) have expressed keen interest in joining this initiative. Dr. Prabhu has co-founded startups including Planys (submersible robots), Solinas (robotics for water/sanitation) and Xyma (high temperature ultrasonic sensors) that are disrupting the asset integrity monitoring space with deep industrial and societal impact (for example, Solinas contributes to the elimination of manual scavenging). His work on Blockchain and AI for secure management of critical records is commercialised through Plenome, with applications in healthcare and voting. He also mentors Terraclime (machine learning or ML-based water meters), Matterize (AI in 3D printing), Krishaka (farm automation), Satori (extended reality or XR) and BotForge (robot foundation models). <!-- image --> Dr. Surender's research group works extensively on the valorisation of various waste materials, including construction & demolition (C&D) waste, for sustainable concrete pavement applications. Some notable contributions include identifying key parameters influencing the recyclability of C&D waste; developing a novel technology to extract high-quality materials (stone, sand, and concrete fines) from C&D waste using concentrated solar energy; identifying failure mechanisms in concrete made with reclaimed asphalt pavement; and developing a technology to remove asphalt from aggregates without chemicals. He is also developing India's first test bed facility, called SADAC (Sustainable ADvanced Aggregate Characterisation), to simulate the recycling process in laboratory conditions. The group's focus is currently on reducing water requirements for concrete curing using C&D waste and developing a technology to extract cement from C&D waste. Dr. Sushanta Kumar Panigrahi's research group focuses on impactful and innovative research in the areas of magnesium and aluminium technologies, sheet metal forming, advanced casting, multi-metallic sheet manufacturing and Innovative materials processing. The group has carried out several funded projects, published several international journal papers, and established 16 patented technologies. A few of his first-of-their-kind in-house patented technologies at IIT Madras include: establishing new magnesium casting and rolling technologies, sustainable aluminium and magnesium recycling technologies, advanced multi-metallic composite sheet manufacturing technologies, new superplastic microforming technology for micro component development such as micro gears, micro pins, micro cups, and micro double cups. The group's latest patented casting process received the International Magnesium Award for Innovative Process of the Year-2024, which was awarded for the first time to an Indian team. The Centre of Excellence for Road Safety, in collaboration with MoRTH, launched the Data Driven Hyperlocal Intervention (DDHI) programme to reduce road accidents. Targeting 100 high-risk districts across 17 states, the initiative uses national crash data to identify local causes. It follows a communitydriven approach through district-level Road Safety Councils. Interventions align with the 5E model - Engineering, Enforcement, Education, Emergency Care, and Empathy. The programme is supported by data from the eDAR system and the Sanjaya platform. In the last year, IIT Madras launched a dedicated Centre for Human-Centric AI (CHAI) focusing on integrating ethical AI solutions for the benefit of society; CySTar, a new Centre for Cybersecurity to boost fundamental and applied research that drives innovations in the country in blockchain, security for AI models, cryptography, quantum security, and IoT security; a Centre of Excellence for research in Fluid and Thermal Sciences that will partner with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) in spacecraft and launch vehicle thermal management; and a Centre of Excellence for Zero Emission Trucking (CoEZET) that focuses on initiatives that support achieving 100% zero emission truck penetration by the year 2050 in India. With Music for All as its central theme, the IITM-Maestro Ilaiyaraaja Centre for Music Learning and Research has been launched in collaboration with Maestro Ilaiyaraaja's IMM (Ilaiyaraaja Music Management) and is a significant step in integrating modern technology with music research. A brief sample of the research that our students carry out in various departments is showcased below: At the Department of Aerospace Engineering, Vipin Kumar investigated flame spread over thin cellulosic circular ducts under normal and microgravity, revealing how geometry, flow speed, and fuel type influence flame propagation. His experiments and simulations highlighted the role of char radiation and conduction heat feedback in enhancing flame spread in complex fuel configurations. At the Department of Applied Mechanics and Biomedical Engineering, Nitikesh Prakash developed a dynamic RO filter with enhanced shear, increasing desalination efficiency by 50%; Anu V S Nath explored how inertial particles cluster and trigger flow instabilities, which deepens our understanding of geophysical flows; and Valeti Chanikya focused on aneurysm rupture risk, simulating blood flow and arterial wall deformation through fluid-structure interaction. Lawanya Natarajan from the Department of Biotechnology studied antibiotic resistance mechanisms through structural and kinetic analysis of TipA and AlbA transcription factors, revealing their versatile binding landscapes. At the Department of Civil Engineering, Jahnabi Basu contributed ground motion models for the Himalayan region, aiding seismic hazard assessments and improvements to Indian seismic codes; Sahil Wani developed a coupled model to simulate gas hydrate dissociation and sediment deformation-crucial for energy extraction; and Roouf Un Nabi Dar advanced ballistic design of reinforced concrete panels using both performance-based methods and Bayesian inference. At the Department of Chemical Engineering, Jigar Halpati explored stable halide perovskites for solar energy, investigating how doping and magnetic fields affect performance; CD Balaji's research focused on CO₂ conversion to methanol using efficient catalysts, offering scalable carbon utilization strategies; and Rajput Shubham studied halide perovskites with ferroelectric properties, paving the way for new memory devices. At the Department of Chemistry, Minakshi Altia leveraged the Heyns and Amadori rearrangements to create diverse N-heterocycles from glucose; Gouranga Naskar devised new annulation strategies for synthesising 5-membered carbocycles from simple building blocks; and Minaz Parbin designed palladium-based molecular cages with anisotropic geometry, capable of guest uptake and photochemical response. At the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Aman Nougrahiya introduced a framework for self-stabilising compilers and efficient iterative dataflow analysis (IDFA) generation, reducing the burden of compiler development; Santhini KA tackled flexible quotas in matching theory, developing fairness-aware algorithms under new optimality notions; and Keshav Ranjan worked on two-sided matchings with capacity constraints, designing efficient algorithms for stable and popular outcomes. Pugazhenthi T from the Department of Engineering Design developed a hybrid AI-FEM (finite element method) framework for flaw detection in structures, combining Bayesian inference and machine learning for high accuracy. At the Electrical Engineering Department, Ajay Govindray Shanbhag addressed trap effects in gallium nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs), proposing optimised buffer structures for improved power and thermal performance and Rohan proposed a novel theory for reactive power evaluation, improving single-phase compensation and EV grid integration. Gauri Sreekumar of the Department of Humanities and Social Sciences investigated how climate change drives rural migration, focusing on socio-economic buffers like irrigation access and remittance use. K Bhadra from the Department of Management Studies examined how Indian manufacturers can build sustainability capabilities using dynamic capability theory and empirical insights. At the Department of Mathematics, Sagar Sawant verified Stanley's tree isomorphism conjecture for a new class of trees and extended it to directed graphs using new polynomial tools; Ritesh Khan developed fast algorithms for large-scale N-body simulations; and Rabeetha V studied twisted shift invariant systems and introduced operators preserving such structures, with applications in wavelet systems. <!-- image --> and diagnostics at the single-cell level; and Suvin VS created a semi-analytical fracture model capable of handling complex heterogeneous media across multiple physics. At the Department of Metallurgical and Materials Engineering, Achintya Patra designed high-performance medium-Mn (manganese) steels using calculation of phase diagrams (CALPHAD)-guided optimisation, achieving impressive strength and ductility; Sanjeev Patil advanced bismuth ferrite nano-composites for flexible electronics and environmental sensing; Usha Rani studied heat-treated Ti-6Al-4V (titanium alloy with aluminium and vanadium) processed by additive manufacturing, correlating structure with mechanical and corrosion properties; and Swati Suman developed sustainable red-light photodetectors using metaloxide and dye composites, integrated via biocompatible encapsulation. Prabhu Kumar V, Department of Ocean Engineering, studied the hydrodynamic behaviour of offshore seawater intake wells using experiments and simulations, focusing on mitigating free surface water oscillations (FSWO). His work showed that curtain walls, especially with optimised porosity, significantly reduce FSWO and improve pumping efficiency under varying wave conditions. At the Department of Mechanical Engineering, Rajes Ranjan Ravi tackled the challenges of trepanning advanced materials, crucial for aerospace and defence sectors; Kiran Raj developed machine learning methods to optimise biodiesel feedstock for cleaner, more efficient engines; Gayathri R proposed innovative cell patterning techniques for therapy At the Department of Physics, VG Abhijitha explored lithium-sulphur and aluminium-ion batteries as nextgeneration alternatives to lithium-ion batteries; Renu Yadav developed bio-voltage memristors with novel architectures for low-power computing; Sayan Ghosh investigated lithium lanthanum titanate phosphate electrolytes and their thermal and microstructural properties for solid-state batteries; and Madhura Ghosh Dastidar studied multiphotonic states and entanglement detection for advancing quantum sensing technologies.

IIT Madras launched the AMOLED Research Centre (ARC) to develop the next generation of active-matrix organic light-emitting diode (AMOLED) displays for smartphones, tablets, watches and wearables. It is funded by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India; Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO); and Tata Sons. This Centre will thus support the nation's initiative of developing a display manufacturing industry. The Extraterrestrial Manufacturing (ExTeM) Research Centre at IIT Madras has been at the forefront of India's space research. It is coming up with innovative processes to tackle the challenges of constructing infrastructure, 3D printing tools, and extracting materials crucial for sustainable space exploration. Our Hon'ble Prime Minister of India has mentioned the ExTeM in his Mann Ki Baat address on January 19, 2025. Researchers at the TTK Center for Rehabilitation Research and Device Development (R2D2), in collaboration with CMC Vellore, have developed PLUTO (Plug and Train Robot), a cost-effective and portable robot for hand rehabilitation. This patented technology offers precise therapeutic movements and real-time feedback, ensuring better outcomes for patients with conditions such as stroke, spinal cord injury, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease and post hand-surgery, among others. Researchers from the Centre of Excellence in Sports Science and Analytics (CESSA) have developed an indigenous portable Point-of-Care-Ultrasound Scanner (POCUS) for sports injury diagnosis and management. This research enables onfield diagnosis of injuries and immediate assessment of the extent of injury. Shri Jyotiraditya M Scindia, Hon'ble Minister of Communications and Minister of Development of North Eastern Region, Government of India, visited the fi rst-of-itskind indigenous 5G Testbed and witnessed a demonstration of the indigenous 5G network in the campus. Researchers at the 5G Testbed are currently working on designing and developing 6G technologies in addition to participating in global standardisation activities and developing Indian intellectual property rights (IPRs) in this critical sector. Under the National Quantum Mission of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, the IITM CDoT Samgnya Technologies Foundation (CDoT: Centre for Development of Telematics), a Section 8 company, has been set up at IIT Madras. This Quantum Communication Thematic Hub (T-hub) will focus on establishing India's quantum-secure communication network, deploying quantum key distribution (QKD) infrastructure, and guiding the nation's transition to post-quantum cryptography. The Foundation, in collaboration with industry and academia, aims to develop indigenous quantum solutions and position India as a global leader in secure next-generation technology. Dr. Aravind Kumar Chandiran's research group is working on solar energy storage and has made 20 significant advancements in the area of green hydrogen in the last year. One of the key achievements is the development of a >250 kW hydrogen microgrid in collaboration with Yokogawa Technology India Pvt Ltd. This microgrid mimics the future of renewable energy grids in India and has been established to study and understand energy management among different energy storage systems, to ensure 24×7 energy security. Dr. Chandiran, along with Dr. Raghuram Chetty (Chemical Engineering), Dr. Krishna Vasudevan (Electrical Engg.) and Dr. Muruganandam (Aerospace Engg.) established the Hyundai HTWO Hydrogen Innovation Centre at the IITM Discovery Campus that focuses on carrying out industrial R&D relevant to hydrogen space and enable faster adoption of hydrogen in power and mobility sectors. An Indian Army-IITM Research Centre, a dedicated Centre of Excellence, is being established to harness the potential of the Institute in various technology domains and serve as the nodal point for defence technology development projects and skilling of the personnel of the armed forces. The Centre will enable translational research and develop disruptive technologies for our armed forces indigenously. Dr. Prabhu Rajagopal's research group at the Automation & Data Engineering vertical of the Center for Nondestructive Evaluation (CNDE) focused on improved diagnostics through metamaterial-enhanced sensors, robotics, AI, quantum and distributed ledger technologies. Last year, Dr. Prabhu's group demonstrated bulk ultrasonic imaging down to an extraordinary resolution of 50 micrometres using micro-structured metalenses. His group is developing the Shobot suite of AI-enabled human collaborative robots for applications ranging from manufacturing and shopping assistance to geriatric homecare. Dr. Prabhu has published one of the first implementations of quantum machine learning for practical ultrasonic material diagnostics. His work on blockchain-based secure management of medical records has also gained wide appreciation. The Centre of Excellence (CoE) on NDE 5.0 (nondestructive evaluation) has launched the pioneering National Consortium for NDE (NCNDE) to promote translational research and product development for sensing and diagnostics; several multinational corporations (MNCs) and national industry majors such as Chevron, Waygate, Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) have expressed keen interest in joining this initiative. Dr. Prabhu has co-founded startups including Planys (submersible robots), Solinas (robotics for water/sanitation) and Xyma (high temperature ultrasonic sensors) that are disrupting the asset integrity monitoring space with deep industrial and societal impact (for example, Solinas contributes to the elimination of manual scavenging). His work on Blockchain and AI for secure management of critical records is commercialised through Plenome, with applications in healthcare and voting. He also mentors Terraclime (machine learning or ML-based water meters), Matterize (AI in 3D printing), Krishaka (farm automation), Satori (extended reality or XR) and BotForge (robot foundation models). <!-- image --> Dr. Surender's research group works extensively on the valorisation of various waste materials, including construction & demolition (C&D) waste, for sustainable concrete pavement applications. Some notable contributions include identifying key parameters influencing the recyclability of C&D waste; developing a novel technology to extract high-quality materials (stone, sand, and concrete fines) from C&D waste using concentrated solar energy; identifying failure mechanisms in concrete made with reclaimed asphalt pavement; and developing a technology to remove asphalt from aggregates without chemicals. He is also developing India's first test bed facility, called SADAC (Sustainable ADvanced Aggregate Characterisation), to simulate the recycling process in laboratory conditions. The group's focus is currently on reducing water requirements for concrete curing using C&D waste and developing a technology to extract cement from C&D waste. Dr. Sushanta Kumar Panigrahi's research group focuses on impactful and innovative research in the areas of magnesium and aluminium technologies, sheet metal forming, advanced casting, multi-metallic sheet manufacturing and Innovative materials processing. The group has carried out several funded projects, published several international journal papers, and established 16 patented technologies. A few of his first-of-their-kind in-house patented technologies at IIT Madras include: establishing new magnesium casting and rolling technologies, sustainable aluminium and magnesium recycling technologies, advanced multi-metallic composite sheet manufacturing technologies, new superplastic microforming technology for micro component development such as micro gears, micro pins, micro cups, and micro double cups. The group's latest patented casting process received the International Magnesium Award for Innovative Process of the Year-2024, which was awarded for the first time to an Indian team. The Centre of Excellence for Road Safety, in collaboration with MoRTH, launched the Data Driven Hyperlocal Intervention (DDHI) programme to reduce road accidents. Targeting 100 high-risk districts across 17 states, the initiative uses national crash data to identify local causes. It follows a communitydriven approach through district-level Road Safety Councils. Interventions align with the 5E model - Engineering, Enforcement, Education, Emergency Care, and Empathy. The programme is supported by data from the eDAR system and the Sanjaya platform. In the last year, IIT Madras launched a dedicated Centre for Human-Centric AI (CHAI) focusing on integrating ethical AI solutions for the benefit of society; CySTar, a new Centre for Cybersecurity to boost fundamental and applied research that drives innovations in the country in blockchain, security for AI models, cryptography, quantum security, and IoT security; a Centre of Excellence for research in Fluid and Thermal Sciences that will partner with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) in spacecraft and launch vehicle thermal management; and a Centre of Excellence for Zero Emission Trucking (CoEZET) that focuses on initiatives that support achieving 100% zero emission truck penetration by the year 2050 in India. With Music for All as its central theme, the IITM-Maestro Ilaiyaraaja Centre for Music Learning and Research has been launched in collaboration with Maestro Ilaiyaraaja's IMM (Ilaiyaraaja Music Management) and is a significant step in integrating modern technology with music research. A brief sample of the research that our students carry out in various departments is showcased below: At the Department of Aerospace Engineering, Vipin Kumar investigated flame spread over thin cellulosic circular ducts under normal and microgravity, revealing how geometry, flow speed, and fuel type influence flame propagation. His experiments and simulations highlighted the role of char radiation and conduction heat feedback in enhancing flame spread in complex fuel configurations. At the Department of Applied Mechanics and Biomedical Engineering, Nitikesh Prakash developed a dynamic RO filter with enhanced shear, increasing desalination efficiency by 50%; Anu V S Nath explored how inertial particles cluster and trigger flow instabilities, which deepens our understanding of geophysical flows; and Valeti Chanikya focused on aneurysm rupture risk, simulating blood flow and arterial wall deformation through fluid-structure interaction. Lawanya Natarajan from the Department of Biotechnology studied antibiotic resistance mechanisms through structural and kinetic analysis of TipA and AlbA transcription factors, revealing their versatile binding landscapes. At the Department of Civil Engineering, Jahnabi Basu contributed ground motion models for the Himalayan region, aiding seismic hazard assessments and improvements to Indian seismic codes; Sahil Wani developed a coupled model to simulate gas hydrate dissociation and sediment deformation-crucial for energy extraction; and Roouf Un Nabi Dar advanced ballistic design of reinforced concrete panels using both performance-based methods and Bayesian inference. At the Department of Chemical Engineering, Jigar Halpati explored stable halide perovskites for solar energy, investigating how doping and magnetic fields affect performance; CD Balaji's research focused on CO₂ conversion to methanol using efficient catalysts, offering scalable carbon utilization strategies; and Rajput Shubham studied halide perovskites with ferroelectric properties, paving the way for new memory devices. At the Department of Chemistry, Minakshi Altia leveraged the Heyns and Amadori rearrangements to create diverse N-heterocycles from glucose; Gouranga Naskar devised new annulation strategies for synthesising 5-membered carbocycles from simple building blocks; and Minaz Parbin designed palladium-based molecular cages with anisotropic geometry, capable of guest uptake and photochemical response. At the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Aman Nougrahiya introduced a framework for self-stabilising compilers and efficient iterative dataflow analysis (IDFA) generation, reducing the burden of compiler development; Santhini KA tackled flexible quotas in matching theory, developing fairness-aware algorithms under new optimality notions; and Keshav Ranjan worked on two-sided matchings with capacity constraints, designing efficient algorithms for stable and popular outcomes. Pugazhenthi T from the Department of Engineering Design developed a hybrid AI-FEM (finite element method) framework for flaw detection in structures, combining Bayesian inference and machine learning for high accuracy. At the Electrical Engineering Department, Ajay Govindray Shanbhag addressed trap effects in gallium nitride (GaN) high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs), proposing optimised buffer structures for improved power and thermal performance and Rohan proposed a novel theory for reactive power evaluation, improving single-phase compensation and EV grid integration. Gauri Sreekumar of the Department of Humanities and Social Sciences investigated how climate change drives rural migration, focusing on socio-economic buffers like irrigation access and remittance use. K Bhadra from the Department of Management Studies examined how Indian manufacturers can build sustainability capabilities using dynamic capability theory and empirical insights. At the Department of Mathematics, Sagar Sawant verified Stanley's tree isomorphism conjecture for a new class of trees and extended it to directed graphs using new polynomial tools; Ritesh Khan developed fast algorithms for large-scale N-body simulations; and Rabeetha V studied twisted shift invariant systems and introduced operators preserving such structures, with applications in wavelet systems. <!-- image --> and diagnostics at the single-cell level; and Suvin VS created a semi-analytical fracture model capable of handling complex heterogeneous media across multiple physics. At the Department of Metallurgical and Materials Engineering, Achintya Patra designed high-performance medium-Mn (manganese) steels using calculation of phase diagrams (CALPHAD)-guided optimisation, achieving impressive strength and ductility; Sanjeev Patil advanced bismuth ferrite nano-composites for flexible electronics and environmental sensing; Usha Rani studied heat-treated Ti-6Al-4V (titanium alloy with aluminium and vanadium) processed by additive manufacturing, correlating structure with mechanical and corrosion properties; and Swati Suman developed sustainable red-light photodetectors using metaloxide and dye composites, integrated via biocompatible encapsulation. Prabhu Kumar V, Department of Ocean Engineering, studied the hydrodynamic behaviour of offshore seawater intake wells using experiments and simulations, focusing on mitigating free surface water oscillations (FSWO). His work showed that curtain walls, especially with optimised porosity, significantly reduce FSWO and improve pumping efficiency under varying wave conditions. At the Department of Mechanical Engineering, Rajes Ranjan Ravi tackled the challenges of trepanning advanced materials, crucial for aerospace and defence sectors; Kiran Raj developed machine learning methods to optimise biodiesel feedstock for cleaner, more efficient engines; Gayathri R proposed innovative cell patterning techniques for therapy At the Department of Physics, VG Abhijitha explored lithium-sulphur and aluminium-ion batteries as nextgeneration alternatives to lithium-ion batteries; Renu Yadav developed bio-voltage memristors with novel architectures for low-power computing; Sayan Ghosh investigated lithium lanthanum titanate phosphate electrolytes and their thermal and microstructural properties for solid-state batteries; and Madhura Ghosh Dastidar studied multiphotonic states and entanglement detection for advancing quantum sensing technologies.

heading: 1.2.2. Institute of Eminence Research Centres
plain_text: ## 1.2.2. Institute of Eminence Research Centres Since being bestowed Institute of Eminence (IoE) status in 2019, IIT Madras has leveraged the strengths of her research groups in addressing new problems with significant potential for breakthroughs in knowledge and applications through her 15 interdisciplinary IoE Centres of Excellence, established in 2023, that span diverse areas of research, including complex systems, industrial asset management, molecular materials, low-carbon construction, healthcare, quantum information, sports science, soft matter studies, and cancer genomics. These Centres of Excellence have positioned themselves as global leaders within their respective fields, with over 50 publications in prestigious journals such as Nature, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences (PNAS), and others. Notably, IITM has received invitations to NVIDIA conferences on two occasions and has graced the cover page of CHasos twice. The CoEs have also organised India's firstever conferences in their domains. Among their notable achievements is HTIC's innovative DHARINI 3D brain model and artesent+. The CoE on Technologies for Low Carbon and Lean Construction (TLC2) has led the way in establishing India's first test bed for recycled aggregates. The Quantum Center for Diamond and Emergent Materials (QuCenDiEM) is providing cutting-edge infrastructure while also advancing diamond-based hardware for quantum computing and communication. They are also working on the first millikelvin measurement at IITM and developing India's inaugural quantum diamond foundry. This foundry, in collaboration with Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), will play a vital role in the National Quantum Mission. NDE 5.0 is driving advancements across various fields. In the area of cancer, the Cancer Genomics Centre has established India's first comprehensive cancer database, the Bharat Cancer Genome Atlas. Furthermore, the CoE for Critical Transitions in Complex Systems (CoE-CTCS) is making significant contributions to India's initiatives in energy, space security, and climate resilience, all while working towards a Viksit Bharat; and the CoE on Maritime Experiments To Maritime Experience (ME2ME) has an in-house wave-maker and wave gauges, and the wave basin facility is indeed one of the largest in the world. Four centres have established consortia: The Energy Consortium (EC), QuCenDiEM, TLC2, and NDE. The IoE mobility programme has supported over 300 international faculty, post-doctoral fellows, and graduate students from 30+ different countries to travel to IIT Madras. IoE funding has played a pivotal role in bolstering state-ofthe-art infrastructure and research facilities, empowering researchers to work on global problems at home. <!-- image -->

heading: 1.2.3. New Research Facilities
plain_text: ## 1.2.3. New Research Facilities IIT Madras continually enhances her research infrastructure to empower scholars and students to pursue cutting-edge research. Notable additions and upgrades made this year include: IIT Madras has partnered with IDBI Bank to launch a Cybersecurity Lab to develop and deploy security solutions in crucial sectors such as healthcare, fintech and aerospace, among others. The lab will focus on creating market-ready IPs in cybersecurity and the productisation and commercialisation of research work, especially for mobile technologies. Some of the major equipment that have been added to the common research infrastructure are: X-ray photoelectron spectrometer (XPS) with ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy (UPS); inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS); high-resolution Fourier-transform nuclear magnetic resonance (FT-NMR) spectrometer, 400 MHz (megahertz); ultra high-resolution electron beam lithography system (EBL); variable pressure high-resolution scanning electron microscope (VPSEM) with energy dispersive spectroscopy for study of conducting, non-conducting and biological samples; high-resolution field emission scanning electron microscope (FESEM) with an in situ tensioncompression testing attachment; high precision automated scratch tester; transmission electron microscopy (Talos F200S G2), 200 kV; and focused ion beam facility (Helios DualBeam). Dr. Shivkumar Kalyanaraman, CEO, Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) inaugurated the following research infrastructure in the Department of Chemistry in April 2025, that will enable students to carry out worldclass research: 500 MHz nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectrometer (Bruker AVNEO), high-resolution mass spectrometer (HRMS) (Waters Xevo G3 Qtof), highresolution travelling electron microscope (HR-TEM) (JEOL Asia Pvt. Ltd.), inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometer ICP (5800 VDV ICP-OES), single crystal X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, multiport BET (Brunauer, Emmett, and Teller) surface area analyser, thermo-gravimetric analysis and differential scanning calorimetry, isothermal thermal calorimeter (MicroCal Mannal PEAQ-ITC), gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), and an automated protein purification system with fast protein liquid chromatography (FPLC). IIT Madras has established Asia's largest shallow wave basin at her Discovery Campus located in Thaiyur to drive research in marine and coastal engineering, a crucial initiative in addressing climate change challenges.

heading: 1.2.5. Industrial Consultancy and Sponsored Research
plain_text: ## 1.2.5. Industrial Consultancy and Sponsored Research The Centre for Industrial Consultancy and Sponsored Research (IC&SR) continues to play a pivotal role in advancing the Institute's research and innovation ecosystem. It not only mobilises funding from various ministries and industries to support research and consultancy activities, but also actively facilitates the protection and transfer of intellectual property by assisting our faculty and students in patenting and commercialising their innovations. In 2024-25, the Institute received sanction for 302 sponsored projects with a total value of INR 317.99 crore, mostly funded by government agencies. Our strong industry collaboration is evident from the 982 consultancy and industry-sponsored research projects received this financial year, amounting to INR 906.41 crore. The above is inclusive of around 70 international projects funded by foreign entities. A brief of some of the major projects undertaken are: Department of Science and Technology (DST) sanctioned INR 30.86 crore for the Shakti SoC test tapeout with 64-bit OoO (out of order) core and AI/ML accelerator under the National Supercomputing Mission; Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) sanctioned INR 25.08 crore for the Integrated Surgical Platform for Total Knee Arthroplasty ; Ministry of Earth Sciences sanctioned INR 11.70 crore for AUV development with homing and docking station under the Deep Ocean Mission; National Technical Research Organisation (NTRO) sanctioned INR 10.52 crore for Demodulation of Complex Waveforms; DST (Fund for Improvement of Science & Technology Infrastructure-FIST Programme 2024) sanctioned INR 5.57 crore to augment research infrastructure in the Chemistry Department over five years; Ministry of Education (Scheme for Promotion of Academic and Research Collaboration, or SPARC) sanctioned INR 5.65 crore for 9 international collaborative research projects across engineering disciplines; Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) sanctioned INR 1.84 crore for the S Ramakrishnan Centre of Excellence for Fluid and Thermal Sciences; Hyundai Motor India Ltd. with Guidance Tamil Nadu sanctioned INR 100 crore for the Hydrogen Valley Innovation Hub at Discovery Campus and HSBC sanctioned INR 21.26 crore for a Centre on Resource Efficiency and Circularity in Energy Transition . This year, IIT Madras has exceeded its target of one patent a day by filing 417 patents, of which 119 are international filings; IIT Madras researchers were granted 207 Indian and 14 international patents. The IC&SR Office has also assisted faculty and students in transferring the technologies developed in labs, and has earned INR 7.03 crore through technology transfer fees and royalties this year. IIT Madras hosted Iinventive, the R&D Innovation Fair of Higher Education Institutes of India from February 28 to March 1, 2025, where around 42 top-ranked NIRF institutions in the Engineering category came together to showcase their cutting-edge research. Our Hon'ble Union Education Minister Shri Dharmendra Pradhan attended the event virtually. The event was inaugurated by the Hon'ble Minister of State for Education, Government of India, Dr. Sukanta Majumdar. During this occasion, two coffee table books were released: Prabhav - From Ideas to Impact, a coffee table book comprising the leading technological innovations impacting industry, and a book on one year of SWAYAM Plus.

heading: 1.3. Research Park and our Deep Tech Startup Incubation System
plain_text: ## 1.3. Research Park and our Deep Tech Startup Incubation System IIT Madras continues to be at the forefront of India's deep tech revolution, with the IITM Incubation Cell (IITMIC) serving as the nucleus of this thriving ecosystem. Over the past 12 years, the IITMIC has nurtured 472 science and engineeringled, IP-driven startups with a combined valuation exceeding INR 50,000 crore (USD 6 billion). These ventures span diverse sectors such as robotics, manufacturing, IoT, mobility, energy, healthcare, biotech, and agri-tech, and are founded by IITM faculty, students, alumni, staff, and external entrepreneurs from across India. Significantly, 28% of these startups have women co-founders, and 30% involve IITM faculty as cofounders or shareholders. Among its notable successes is Ather Energy, co-founded by IITM alumni Tarun Mehta and Swapnil Jain, which became IITMIC's first IPO-listed company on May 6, 2025, valued at INR 11,956 crore (USD 1.5 billion). This milestone follows the emergence of two unicorns from the IITMIC portfolio. Other noteworthy IITMIC startups include Uniphore, Agnikul, MediBuddy, NeoMotion, Solinas, Mindgrove, Xyma Analytics, The ePlane Company, and GalaxEye. Today, 190 IITMIC startups are actively generating INR 4,000 crore in annual revenue, creating over 11,000 direct jobs, and filing more than 700 patents. With an impressive 80% survival rate, these startups reflect the robustness of IIT Madras' deep tech innovation model-one built on advanced engineering, scalable technologies, and real-world impact. As mentioned earlier, in alignment with the 'Startup 100 Mission' launched in early 2024, the IITM Incubation Cell achieved a historic milestone in FY 2024-25, incubating <!-- image --> 103 new deep tech startups -the highest in any single year since its inception. This milestone, called 'Startup Shatam' , was made possible through the collaborative efforts of IITMIC and IITM's sector-specific incubators (including HTIC MedTech, Pravartak, Bioincubator, and RTBI ), the School of Innovation & Entrepreneurship (which houses IITM's preincubator Nirmaan and the Centre for Innovation or CFI), and engaging with 700+ entrepreneurs across India during the year. The ePlane Company, incubated at IIT Madras and developer of electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft, has become the first private Indian company to receive formal acceptance from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) for the type certification of its eVTOL aircraft, the e200X. It has completed flight tests of its subscale prototype in March 2025, and their first full-scale air taxi prototype is under production and is expected to be ready by the end of September 2025. heading: 1.4. International Collaborations
plain_text: ## 1.4. International Collaborations The Office of Global Engagement (OGE) at IIT Madras has continued to play a pivotal role in strengthening the Institute's international presence by facilitating collaborations, scholar exchanges, and delegation visits from universities and embassies. In the academic year 2024-2025, IIT Madras signed 14 new MoUs and renewed 17 existing ones, bringing the total number of active MoUs to approximately 378. These agreements have enabled a wide range of international academic and research collaborations. Under International Student Activities, IIT Madras welcomed 51 full-time international students across various postgraduate programmes. This comprises 40 students enrolled in master's programmes, 2 in PhD programmes, and 9 in MS programmes, reflecting the Institute's growing global appeal and commitment to fostering a diverse academic community. Through the AARDO-IITM Scholarship, 24 faculty members submitted proposals, and 9 international students were selected for the MS programme, working across projects focused on technology and rural development in Asia and Africa. IIT Madras continues to expand its Joint Master's Programs in collaboration with reputed international universities. In 2024, 28 students enrolled in the Joint MSc in Data Science & AI with the University of Birmingham, 10 students in the Sustainable Energy Systems programme, and another 10 students in the Water Security & Global Change programme offered with RWTH Aachen, TU Dresden, and the Global Water and Climate Adaptation Centre-Aachen, Bangkok, Chennai, Dresden (ABCD Centre). The Joint Doctoral Programme (JDP) allows PhD scholars to spend 12-18 months at one of 19 partner institutions. In 2024-25, two inbound students, including one from Azerbaijan, joined IITM, and 16 IITM scholars completed joint PhDs at institutes across Singapore, Australia, Germany, France, and the USA . The Agriculture Stack Architecture) platform, and VR-based STEM education in rural schools. IIT Madras signed an MoU with the Auroville Foundation a few days ago to set up the Auroville Foundation-IIT Madras Sustainability Campus on a 100-acre plot allocated by Auroville. The sustainable campus will serve as a model of regenerative design, zero-carbon infrastructure and inclusive, climate-resilient development. It aims to become a global hub for interdisciplinary research and technological solutions focussed on clean energy, circular economy, water conservation, sustainable urbanisation and community wellbeing. IITM and IITMIC remain deeply committed to building a robust, innovation-driven ecosystem that enables startups to solve complex societal challenges, facilitate job creation, and contribute to India's leadership in deep-tech entrepreneurship. IIT Madras is about to catalyse the setting up of a Series A and pre-Series A-focused venture capital fund. Alumni and other high-net-worth individuals (HNIs) can invest in this fund. The fund will in turn make investments in our startups. Through this mechanism we hope to scale up the impact that our startups will have and ensure that our alumni and wellwishers can also participate in and fuel our success. With this we expect to see many more of our startups scaling. newly launched IITM-Deakin Academy also saw 11 students enrolled under this global JDP initiative. Inbound mobility remained strong, with IIT Madras hosting 72 semester exchange students from Spain, Germany, France, Sweden, and Taiwan. These students were supported through structured orientation programmes, academic guidance, and cultural immersion activities on campus. In addition, 73 short-term international students visited the Institute under various programmes such as internships, Fulbright, Indo-German Centre for Sustainability (IGCS), IoE, International Research Skills Program for Developing Sustainable Transportation System and Infrastructure (STSI), National Science Foundation International Research Experiences for Students (NSF IRES), Institute of International Education (IIE), CV Raman Fellowship, and the India-Science Research Fellowship (ISRF), participating in research work and academic exchanges. On the outbound front, 32 IITM undergraduate and postgraduate students participated in the Semester Exchange Programme, gaining academic exposure at leading global universities. Students also secured placements in prestigious internships and summer programmes, including Nanyang Technological University (NTU) Singapore's Global Connect Fellowship, the Australian National University's Future Research Talent Awards, the National University of Singapore (NUS) Young Fellowship, Tokyo Tech's Asia-Oceania Top University League on Engineering (AOTULE) Summer Program, École Polytechnique's International Talents Program, the Sakura Science Program, the Kyoto University Short-Term Academic Research (KU-STAR) Program, the Global Youth Leadership Program (GYLP), and the Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH) Summer Program. Additionally, IITM welcomed students on study visits from our partner universities, offering rich cultural and academic exposure. These included two visits from the Shibaura Institute of Technology, Japan (in August 2024 and again in February-March 2025), and one visit each from the BavarianIndian Centre for Business and University Cooperation (BayIND), Germany in September 2024, Auckland University of Technology, New Zealand in November 2024, and the University of Tokyo, Japan in February 2025.

Some major infrastructure projects that have been successfully completed this year at a cost of around INR 205 crore are: New Academic Complex II; Pothigai (Director's Bungalow); CCTV surveillance in Hostel and Institute zones; Gas Dynamics Lab; archive facility; and fixing grills in Ganga hostel. The Hospital renovation and restructuring was completed with generous donations from the Batch of 1976 alumni and the IIT Madras Alumni Association of North America, and was inaugurated on December 11. A state-of-the-art Sitara Indoor Sports Complex was inaugurated on November 4, 2024.

heading: 1.7. Sustainability
plain_text: ## 1.7. Sustainability The School of Sustainability (SoS) was inaugurated in October 2023 by Shri Jayant Sinha, the erstwhile Member of Parliament and Chairperson, Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance. In under two years, the SoS has grown to be a vibrant space for capacity building, actionable research, and active stakeholder engagement in diverse domains of sustainability. Its journey so far includes launching three undergraduate & executive educational programs, initiating eight research projects, organising 10+ national and international convenings, and contributing to six research publications-all towards ensuring a multi-dimensional perspective on sustainability. SoS, in addition to a Minor in Sustainability that is offered to all undergraduate students, offers a range of interdisciplinary courses-the most popular one among students being the hands-on course 'Sustainability and Entrepreneurship'. The online certificate programme 'Sustainability for Indian Businesses' has seen the enrolment of over 150 working professionals from varied industries. With interdisciplinarity as its mantra, the SoS pursues actionable research bridging gaps among science, policy The International Immersion Experience (IIE) programme enabled 36 PhD scholars to undertake short-term research visits in 16 countries, collaborating with premier institutions such as MIT, Stanford University, and the National University of Singapore. Some major projects that are ongoing at a cost of about INR 240 crore are: Hostel Block and Academic Research Block at Discovery Campus; Staff Housing; centralised chilled water systems; IITM-Maestro Ilaiyaraaja Centre for Music Learning and Research; renovation of various sports facilities; installation of solar power plants; replacement of lifts in various buildings; and establishment of a biogas plant. heading: 1.8. Student Co-Curricular and Extra-Curricular Activities
plain_text: ## 1.8. Student Co-Curricular and Extra-Curricular Activities IIT Madras continues to shine through vibrant student initiatives and landmark achievements. Shaastra, the technical festival held from January 3-7, 2025 was graced by distinguished personalities: Dr. Sujatha Ramdorai, Smt. Ruchira Kamboj, Dr. Arokiaswamy Velumani, and Mr. Nambi Narayanan. With a lineup of 80 events such as 'Rewire', a cognitive enhancement initiative, and 'Uzhavu', a social campaign for sustainable agriculture, competitions like Robowars and Laser Tag, and a vibrant lineup of workshops, Shaastra 2025 reaffirmed its status as India's largest studentrun technical festival, exemplifying innovation, excellence, and societal impact. Saarang, celebrating the golden jubilee this year (tracing its origins back to its inception as Mardi Gras in 1974), was held from January 9-13, 2025. It featured over 100 events, drew more than 10,000 student participants, and witnessed a footfall of 80,000+ and a revenue generation of around INR 1.8 crore, reaffirming its stature as one of India's largest studentorganised cultural festivals. The Classical Night paid tribute to India's artistic heritage and was graced by two legendary personalitiesIsaignani Ilaiyaraaja and the Hon'ble Governor of Tamil Nadu, Thiru RN Ravi . The Professional Shows mesmerised audiences, the Spotlight Lecture Series featured meaningful interactions, and the vibrant World Fest added global flavour-all reflecting this year's central theme: Cinema. The Extramural Lecture Series (EML) featured speakers from diverse fields, including Satyajit Padhye, Lt. Gen. Satish Dua, Divya Goswami, Vinay Varanasi, and Sudhanshu Rai. Collaborating with groups like Saathi and the Chess Club, EML also brought in noted personalities such as the late Dr. R Chidambaram, Dr. Shekhar Seshadri, chess champion D Gukesh, Pt. Rakesh Chaurasia, activist Prashant Bhushan, and IPS officer Sadanand Date. CFI teams achieved remarkable success across global platforms. Team Abhyuday ranked 11 th globally and 1 st in Asia at the Spaceport America Cup 2025, also winning a Judge's Recognition Award. Team Abhiyaan was placed 8 th overall and 6 th in Design at Intelligent Ground Vehicle Competition (IGVC) 2024 with their autonomous vehicle Vidyut . Team Raftar secured 2 nd in the Electric Vehicle (EV) category at Formula Bharat 2024, winning top design awards including Best Engineering Design and Best Battery Design. Team Abhiyaan achieved their personal best at IGVC 2024 with Vidyut , navigating 114 feet autonomously and securing 6 th place in the Design Challenge and 8 th overall. Team Anveshak achieved 2 nd place at the International Rover Challenge 2024, earning the 'Autonomous Masters' and 'Excellence in Autonomous Mission' titles. Team Amogh ranked among the top 40 globally at the Singapore AUV (Autonomous Underwater Vehicle) Challenge and was placed 9 th in the qualification task. Tvasta, from the 3D Printing Club, was one of eight startups to present before the Prime Minister and now operates independently in Bengaluru. Team Agnirath has developed Aagneya , a fully solar-powered electric vehicle that will represent India in the Bridgestone World Solar Challenge 2025 from Darwin to Adelaide, Australia. Team Sahaay's Pestocart earned a design patent. The Aero Club achieved 3rd place nationally in the Society of Automotive Engineers India (SAEINDIA) Aerothon and won an Inter-IIT gold medal for their vision-based obstacle avoidance drone in a DRDO problem statement challenge. Their project GAIA also secured 4th place among 200+ teams at a national robotics competition. The Hon'ble Minister for Railways, Information and Broadcasting, Electronics & Information Technology, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, visited IIT Madras's Hyperloop Facility, Asia's longest operational student-run hyperloop test facility of 422 metres, where Asia's first Global Hyperloop competition was hosted earlier this year. Entrepreneurship Summit (E-Summit'25), held from February 28 to March 2, 2025, celebrated a Decade of Dynamism . The summit served as a platform for aspiring entrepreneurs to engage with industry experts, venture capitalists, and peers, fostering innovation and the growth of viable business ventures. The All-India Research Scholars Summit (AIRSS), an event designed by and for research scholars to celebrate innovation, collaboration, and scholarly excellence, was held in March 2025 and served as a platform to present cutting-edge research, spark new ideas, and foster peer learning. IIT Madras sports teams delivered stellar performances this year. At the 57 th Inter IIT Sports Meet, IIT Madras secured the Overall General Championship Runner-Up, with the women's contingent clinching the Women's General Championship consecutively for the 2 nd time and the men's contingent finishing 4 th in the Men's General Champions. The IITM contingent won one gold, four silver and six bronze Medals. Notable athletics performances included golds by Visveshwar (400m race), Gaurav Yadav (pole vault, also setting an Inter-IIT record), and Vetrichelvan (triple jump), along with multiple other podium finishes in individual and relay events. Eugene Vincent K was named Best Lifter and set a new Inter-IIT record in weightlifting, while Nandini Jain was awarded Most Valuable Player (MVP) in women's squash. At the 38 th Inter-IIT Aquatics Meet, the women's team emerged Runner-Up. IIT Madras proudly hosted Virasat 2025, the 10 th Annual International Convention of the Society for the Promotion of Indian Classical Music And Culture Amongst Youth (SPIC MACAY) in March. The event celebrated India's rich classical heritage through performances by legends like Padma Shri Pt. Dr. S Ballesh Bhajantri, Pt. Sanjeev Abhyankar, Vid. Ramakrishnan Murthy, Vid. Trichur V Ramachandran, Dr. Thiruvarur Bakthavatchalam, Pt. Nayan Ghosh, Guru M Badrappan, and Vid. Narthaki Nataraj. In addition to concerts, immersive workshops and cultural sessions engaged students deeply. Together, these initiatives reflect the diversity, brilliance, and leadership of IIT Madras students across all fronts-technology, entrepreneurship, sports, arts, and social impact. <!-- image -->

heading: 1.9. Students' Welfare
plain_text: ## 1.9. Students' Welfare IIT Madras ensures a safe, supportive, and happy campus by prioritising holistic student wellness-physical, mental, social, and economic. As a key initiative, all freshers undergo a wellness survey, supported by experts, to identify early needs. Counsellors are available in hostels, departments, hospital, and the Wellness Centre. MITR and Saathi, the Institute's wellness support group, organised several events like the Annual Wellness Drive, including a 5K Marathon, sleep therapy and anger management workshops, blindfold conversations with MYRafiky, hostel drives, Gatekeeper sessions with Sneha Foundation and vibrant evenings like DJ and games nights, to strengthen peer support.

heading: 1.11. Alumni Matters
plain_text: ## 1.11. Alumni Matters In 2025, we honoured ten of our alumni with the Distinguished Alumnus Award for outstanding achievements in their respective fields. They are Dr. Ramesh K Sitaraman, Dr. Srinivasan Natarajan, Dr. Sandhya Dwarkadas, Dr. Vijay Narayanan, Shri Sreenivas Subramoney, Dr. S Somanath, Shri Vellayan Subbiah, Shri BK Kameswara Rao, Shri Ramesh Srinivasan and Smt. Jaishree Deshpande. Dr. Swarun Kumar and Dr. Venkatasubramanian Viswanathan have been recognised with Young Alumni Achiever Awards this year. I am extremely happy to share that IITM's Office of Alumni and Corporate Relations and Office of Institutional Advancement have raised INR 320 crore in 2024-25. Of this, INR 124.4 crore was from key alumni and INR 195.20 from CSR donations. Some of the key alumni and philanthropic trust contributors of the year are: Sunil Wadhwani (INR 28.8 crore), Kris Gopalakrishnan (INR 23.8 crore), Prem Watsa (INR 8.31 crore), Anonymous Donors (INR 7.10 crore), Venkat Rangan (INR 4.99 crore), Subramonian Shankar (INR 3.74 crore), Maheshwar Saireddy (INR 2.06 crore), K Vijay (INR 2 crore) and Vijay Janapathy (INR 1.45 crore). The key CSR donors of the year are: NTPC set up a Cardiovascular Centre at the Department of Medical Sciences and Technology; Hyundai boosted IIT Madras's pioneering work in setting up the Hydrogen Valley Innovation Hub at the Thaiyur Discovery Campus and in establishing the Hyundai Centre for Cancer Genomics; FedEx continued to support the Supply Chain Modelling, Algorithms, Research and Technology (SMART) Center to focus on the digital, sustainable and safety aspects of logistics; HSBC supported a centre for circularity and Kushal meetings continue to enable students' interaction with their faculty advisors or guides at regular intervals. The 'Be Happy' portal (behappy.iitm.ac.in) launched in this regard enables students to provide their inputs pertaining to discrimination, problems faced in paper publication/ thesis submissions, non-availability of research equipment etc., enabling early intervention by the Institute in redressing grievances. IIT Madras is deeply committed to inclusive education, ensuring that students with disabilities have equitable access to academics, campus life, and career opportunities. The Inclusive Education Resource Centre, inaugurated last year, has been providing advanced assistive technologies, mobility support, personalised accommodations, and sensitisation programmes, empowering every student to thrive and reach their full potential. CPC and Team Pragati (the Union Public Service Commission or UPSC Club at IITM) initiated a programme last year to actively support students aspiring to join the Indian Civil Services and explore roles in public policy and civil services that will enable building a stronger, more self-reliant nation. energy transition; American Express funded a programme on innovation and entrepreneurship; Power Finance Corp continued their support of the Department of Medical Sciences and Technology's Anatomy Lab for BS Students; Kotak Bank continued to fund the Kotak IIT Save Energy Mission, working with multiple IITs to do energy audits of micro-, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) across geographies to help optimise their energy usage; Prazim Trading supported cutting-edge brain research at the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre; HDFC supported pre-incubation setup for climate action startups; and IDBI Bank helped set up a Cyber Security Lab. As mentioned earlier, a Venture Capital Fund will be created wherein alumni can make investments that will be utilised to scale up the impact of our startups. A Support for Living Expenses (SLE) initiative has been launched this year to cover the hostel and mess fees of students whose annual parental incomes are below INR 1 lakh, thus enabling them to focus on their studies without financial stress. 201 deserving students have benefitted by this scheme. Apart from providing mentoring support to students and contributing to various infrastructure projects (mentioned earlier), alumni have also supported nearly 422 students with scholarships and supported the institution of Chairs and Fellowships. The S Srinivasan Institute Chair and the Prof. Chandramouli Early Career Chair have been instituted this year. Women Leading IITM (WLI) continues to nurture, develop and support the talents of women at IITM in their academic and professional careers. The primary goal of this initiative, running with support from some of our US alumni, is achieving a more gender-balanced and nurturing campus. This year, 37 grantees have been chosen, taking the total number of grantees so far to 150.

Acknowledgements All these activities at scale and accomplishments of our Institute would not have been possible without the committed participation and support of all stakeholders-our faculty, students and staff; agencies and industries sponsoring R&D and consultancy projects; professionals from other organisations who assist us in various capacities; and our alumni and corporate donors with their generous support to our various activities. In particular, I would like to thank officebearers such as Heads of Departments, Deans, Chairpersons, Wardens, Advisors, and Professors-in-charge of various Cells and Centres, and hospital and hostel staff for the selfless work they put in to keep the Institute ticking. The Institute is grateful to the Ministry of Education, Government of India, for its continued and sustained encouragement and support. I also wish to thank the Government of Tamil Nadu for all the support it continues to extend in multiple ways. On behalf of the Institute, I wish to thank, in addition to the above major donors, all our alumni, corporates and wellwishers who have contributed magnanimously and made this achievable. I wish to thank Dr. Pawan Goenka, our Chairman, Board of Governors, and all board members for their wise counsel, support and guidance, enabling us to scale new heights. I would like to express my heartfelt gratitude to our Chief Guest, Shri Ajit Doval, and our Guest of Honour, Dr. Padma Subrahmanyam, for gracing this convocation. We are eager to listen to your message to the graduating class of 2025. Before I end, I would once again like to congratulate the prize-winners today and wish all our graduands happiness, professional success, and fulfilment from a life of service to their profession, family and country. God bless you all. Jai Hind! <!-- image --> <!-- image --> All data pertains to activities between April 1, 2024 and March 31, 2025 unless otherwise specified.

heading: Ongoing Activities of Hindi Cell
plain_text: ## Ongoing Activities of Hindi Cell To ensure effective implementation of the Official Language policy of the Government of India, efforts have been made to maintain a conducive atmosphere for the usage of Hindi in the Institute. The Cell engages in translation of the Institute's Annual Report, Annual Accounts Report and various other documents covered under section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, including name boards, rubber stamps, letterheads, file folders, advertisements (students' admission, teaching and non-teaching positions), press releases, Convocation and Institute Day invitations, etc. Besides, the 'Improve your vocabulary' initiative under the 'Learn a word in Hindi' programme is updated daily through announcement mail in three languages, viz., Tamil, Hindi and English.
