heading: c) Hindi Workshops and Seminars
plain_text: ## c) Hindi Workshops and Seminars In order to solve the difficulties and problems faced by the employees in using Hindi in their daily work, the Hindi Cell organises Hindi workshops for the employees of the Institute every quarter. 100 employees were given training on various topics, including Noting & Drafting in Hindi; Spoken Hindi & Simple Sentence Structure; Hindi in Daily Life-Grammar in Daily Use; Basic Hindi; and Construction of Words and Sentences. heading: 4.3.1. Introduction
plain_text: ## 4.3.1. Introduction The Department of Biotechnology at IIT Madras was founded in 2004 with a vision to be recognised as a department of international repute with a strong interdisciplinary research and teaching base in biological sciences and engineering, involving an active collaboration with industries and health care institutions. The thrust areas of research are biological sciences, bioprocess engineering, computational biology, chemical biology and medical biotechnology related to cancer, neuroscience and cardiovascular aspects. Faculty members of the Department hold several patents and are involved in active industrial consultancy. Over the past decade, the Department has made significant strides in establishing itself as one of the best centres of excellence in the field of Biotechnology. The Department, housed in the Bhupat and Jyoti Mehta School of Biosciences, has a multidisciplinary coverage of scientific, technological, socio-economic, and educational domains of interest. It aspires to become an internationally recognized Centre of Repute, through collaborations with academic institutions, industries, healthcare institutions and other stakeholders. Department of Biotechnology <!-- image --> 4.3. Several collaborative and technology transfer projects are currently underway with various industries and the Department also engages in collaborative research projects with hospitals. A Centre of Excellence in Bioprocess Engineering has been established to develop knowledge and expertise in this domain, besides a Department of Science & Technology (DST)-funded National Facility to Identify Potential Drug Targets through Cellular Dynamics and a Fund for Improvement of S&T Infrastructure (FIST) facility for infrastructure development. The Department of Biotechnology (DBT) funded for a programme support on Cancer Biology earlier and now the DST is supporting a National Cancer Tissue Biobank. A Bioinformatics Centre has also been set up with funding from DBT. IITM Bio-incubator, initiated by our department and funded by the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), offers lab and office space, including equipment, technical support and centralised utilities for process and product development.

heading: 4.4.1. Introduction
plain_text: ## 4.4.1. Introduction Department of Chemical Engineering <!-- image --> 4.4. Chemical engineering is a dynamic field that is continuously evolving to drive global advancements. The Department of Chemical Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IITM), plays a pivotal leadership role in this progress through its modern teaching curriculum, cutting-edge research, active industry collaborations, and entrepreneurial activities. Established in 1959 alongside the Institute, the Department had humble beginnings, benefitting primarily from German collaboration in nearly all its functions. Fast forwarding to the present day, our laboratories employ fully operational large-scale equipment, while keeping pace with ongoing miniaturization and Industry 4.0 trends, prompting continuous updates. The Department's diverse group of faculty members are actively engaged in solving contemporary problems through industrial consultancy, exploring fundamental science, and advancing development towards the future through next-generation technologies--all while leveraging state-of-the-art research and development (R&D) facilities that offer students valuable insights into real-world scientific and industrial settings. Our faculty members are also involved in conducting cutting-edge research across multi-disciplinary fields, including environment, energy & materials, molecular simulations, reaction engineering, process intensification, process systems engineering, artificial intelligence, etc.

heading: 4.5.1. Introduction
plain_text: ## 4.5.1. Introduction Department of Chemistry <!-- image --> 4.5. The Department of Chemistry was a part of the Department of Chemical Engineering from 1959-1961 and became an independent department in 1961 with Prof. V Srinivasan as the Head-in-Charge. Prof. MVC Sastri assumed charge as the first Head of the Department in November 1961. He was instrumental in building the department as well as the Applied Chemistry Building (completed in 1973). Prof. Sastri was also responsible for the Special Instruments Laboratory (established in 1970; later known as Regional Sophisticated Instrumentation Centre (RSIC) and presently known as the Sophisticated Analytical Instrument Facility (SAIF), and the Materials Science Research Centre (MSRC) (established in 1974 with Prof. Sastri as the Head and Prof. V Srinivasan as the Associate Head). The Department offers MSc and PhD programmes in chemistry. As of date, 1253 students have graduated with the MSc degree and 945 students with the PhD degree. Various aspects of chemistry are also taught at the preparatory level (for weaker section students) and in the BTech programme (core as well as minor stream courses in chemistry). The Department is well-equipped with modern instrumentation facilities and actively engaged in performing quality teaching and research in frontier areas.

plain_text: ## 4.6.1. Introduction The Department of Civil Engineering has been in existence since the inception of IIT Madras in 1959. Since then, it has contributed to the nation's infrastructure development and human resource generation. The departmental activities include teaching, research, consultancy, and training. These activities are carried out under different disciplines, administratively organised into six divisions, namely Building Department of Civil Engineering Technology Construction Materials & Management (BTCM), Environmental Engineering (EE), Hydraulics and Water Resources Engineering (HWRE), Geotechnical Engineering (GT), Structural Engineering (ST) and Transportation Engineering (TR). There are 14 well-equipped laboratories attached to these divisions. <!-- image -->

## 4.6.1. Introduction The Department of Civil Engineering has been in existence since the inception of IIT Madras in 1959. Since then, it has contributed to the nation's infrastructure development and human resource generation. The departmental activities include teaching, research, consultancy, and training. These activities are carried out under different disciplines, administratively organised into six divisions, namely Building Department of Civil Engineering Technology Construction Materials & Management (BTCM), Environmental Engineering (EE), Hydraulics and Water Resources Engineering (HWRE), Geotechnical Engineering (GT), Structural Engineering (ST) and Transportation Engineering (TR). There are 14 well-equipped laboratories attached to these divisions. <!-- image -->

heading: 4.6.2. Academic Programmes
plain_text: ## 4.6.2. Academic Programmes The Department has postgraduate programmes leading to Dual Degree, MTech MS and PhD degrees with specialisation in various disciplines of civil engineering in addition to the 4.6. undergraduate BTech programme in civil engineering. Also, the Department offers a user-oriented industry sponsored post-graduate diploma in bridge engineering.

## 4.6.7.2. Socially Relevant Activities 1. National Centre for Safety of Heritage Structures (NCSHS) was involved in the conservation of the 11th century AD Sri Abathsahayeswarar Temple in Thukkatchi, Tamil Nadu. It has been selected for the 2024 UNESCO Asia-Pacific Award of Distinction for Heritage Conservation among 52 projects received from the Asia-Pacific Region by UNESCO Bangkok. An interdisciplinary team prepared the detailed project report in 2022, which was then executed by Thirunavukarasar Arakkalai Trust and HR&CE.

heading: Citation for the 2024 UNESCO Asia-Pacific Award of Distinction for Her
plain_text: ## Citation for the 2024 UNESCO Asia-Pacific Award of Distinction for Heritage Conservation 'The revival of the Abathsahayeshwarar Temple in Tamil Nadu has breathed new life to a once abandoned religious site, employing an interdisciplinary methodology which connects modern conservation science with traditional construction practices. In this spirit, engineering expertise and the knowhow of Hindu temple builders, sthapathi, were applied in structural conservation and renewal of decorative works in keeping with vernacular artisanal traditions. The pedagogical aspiration of the project in establishing guidelines for the restoration of historic living Hindu temples in Tamil Nadu is praiseworthy. Significant support from both the government and devotees has enabled the continuity of this historic temple in a modernday devotional context.' EPFL Switzerland, UCLV Cuba, IIT Delhi and TARA Delhi. The efforts at these institutions led to a rapid adoption of a standard for LC3 in India, and commercial production of the cement is imminent. 2. Geotechnical engineering group of IITM along with Malaviya National Institute of Technology Jaipur (MNITJ) has undertaken the following activities to respond to the Dam Safety Act, 2021: - i. Development of Methods of Hazard, Vulnerability and Exposure estimations, and thereby of estimating Risk related to Flood and Earthquake Hazards in the State of Maharashtra; - ii. Capacity Development of dam engineers of the State of Maharashtra in the domains related to flood and earthquake - iii. Demonstration of Safety Assessment, through Pilot Study of 7 select dams. 3. The centre for low-carbon and lean construction demonstrated the use of concentrated solar energy for thermomechanical beneficiation of concrete from demolition waste for recycling in new structures. They also demonstrated the recyclability potential of demolished concrete in the Chennai Metro Rail project. 4. The pavement engineering group of IITM CE department was involved in the development of IS73 standards for bitumen - first ever project funded by Bureau of Indian Standards, Govt. of India. The group also developed the Warrants for the use of Modified Bitumen for India - funded by DST, Govt of India. They carried out the first-ever systematic study on modified binder characterization and mapped temperature+traffic for all the NH in the country with a choice of modified binder.

heading: StarPlat
plain_text: ## StarPlat In this project funded by the National Supercomputing Mission and Qualcomm, Rupesh Nasre's group has developed a domain-specific language (DSL) for graph algorithms. One can specify a graph algorithm in this DSL at a high level, and the code generators generate parallel code from it for different backends. Currently, the compiler is able to generate code for Open Multi-Processing (OpenMP) (multi-core Central Processing Unit [CPU]), Message Passing Interface (MPI) (for a distributed setup), Compute Unified Device Architecture (CUDA) (for NVIDIA Graphics Processing Unit [GPUs]), OpenACC (accelerators), SYCL (Intel GPUs) and Open Computing Language (OpenCL) (multiple computing platforms) from the same algorithmic specification. The language is mature enough to specify simple graph algorithms such as single- source shortest paths, page rank, betweenness centrality, and triangle counting. Multiple ways in which the group is taking this forward are: improving the efficiency of the generated codes, supporting complex graph algorithms requiring concurrent data structures, supporting more backends such as multi-GPU/Hip, supporting more dynamic graphs, etc. The work is patented and has been made publicly available.

heading: Online Malware Research
plain_text: ## Online Malware Research A key objective in this project is to develop an online forum that facilitates AI-based malware analysis. This platform offers datasets of malware runtime behavior, enabling students and researchers to study malware execution across various platforms, including Linux, Windows, and mobile systems. The project is built on a lightweight heterogeneous testbed framework, called 'JUGAAD', that is designed to build holistic datasets for malware analysis mimicking real-world environments. JUGAAD facilitates large-scale malware analysis by providing a cross-dimensional view of malware behavior and supports the development of novel detection techniques. The project has been extensively tested during a Malware Analysis Hackathon conducted by Centre for Cybersecurity, Trust, and Reliability (CyStar) in August to October 2024. Two patents based on this project have been granted and a third has been filed. The project is funded by Industrial Development Bank of India - Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IDBI-IITM) Secure Systems Laboratory (IDBI-IITM SSL).

heading: Side-Channel Power Leakage Analyzer
plain_text: ## Side-Channel Power Leakage Analyzer This is a tool for early-stage power side-channel analysis of digital circuits at the Register-Transfer Level (RTL) or gate-level. PLAN conducts extensive behavioral simulations to assess correlations between circuit signals and a reference signal, estimating each signal's leakage potential. This facilitates early detection and mitigation of vulnerabilities during the design phase. It has been tested on Reduced Instruction Set Computing (RISC) V processors and has won the best paper award at IEEE International Symposium on Hardware Oriented Security and Trust (HOST) 2020. This project is supported by the Center for Hardware Security Entrepreneurship Research and Development (CHERD), an initiative by the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MEITY). The tool is currently being productized by Vyoma Technologies (an EDA startup) and SecurSi Technologies (a security startup), both incubated at the IIT Madras Research Park.

heading: 4.8.1. Introduction
plain_text: ## 4.8.1. Introduction The Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT Madras) has successfully established the Wadhwani School of Data Science and AI (artificial intelligence) with an endowment of INR 110 crore from Mr. Sunil Wadhwani, CEO of Mastech, Inc. and IGATE, and a proud alumnus of IITM. Founded in 2024, the school brings together several faculty members with expertise in various areas of data science and AI to collaborate on impactful problems of direct societal relevance. The school is home to the Institute's 18th and newest department. Department of Data Science & Artificial Intelligence 4.8. It has several affiliated research centres, such as the Robert Bosch Centre for Data Science and Artificial Intelligence (RBCDSAI), Centre for Responsible AI (CeRAI), Centre for Integrative Biology and Systems medicinE (IBSE), AI4Bharat, and a vibrant research ecosystem, with several interest groups focused on exciting areas. The school will also offer a BTech in AI & Data Analytics, an MTech in Data Science and AI, and multiple programmes for international students. The school will enable close collaboration between domain experts and AI researchers to enable solutions that integrate AI with existing domain knowledge and approaches. The degree programmes will nurture the students to primarily think in terms of interdisciplinary design and data-driven problemsolving. Overall, our vision is to create an environment for globally competitive research and teaching, and ultimately place the school amongst the top centres in the world for research in three key areas, with a special emphasis on AI for Healthcare, in the Indian context.

heading: 4.8.6.1. Mobility and Intelligent Transportation (MINT)
plain_text: ## 4.8.6.1. Mobility and Intelligent Transportation (MINT) Launched on April 4, 2024 MINT is a global initiative to build mobility digital infrastructure and a research and development (R&D) portfolio, besides developing a skilled workforce to develop breakthrough mobility solutions to realize the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), such as - Sustainable Transport (11.2): 50% reduction in total transport emissions - Accident Prevention (3.6): 50% reduction in fatalities - Energy Efficiency (7.3): 50% of all transport from net zero modes <!-- image -->

heading: 4.9.1. Introduction
plain_text: ## 4.9.1. Introduction Established in 2006, the Department of Engineering Design (ED) is the 16th department to come up at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras. Engineering design is a structured process that engineers follow to solve a problem. Often, this solution involves designing a product that fulfils certain criteria and/or accomplishes a certain task. It is a decision-making process, often iterative, wherein the principles of basic and engineering sciences are applied to optimise the conversion of resources to meet a stated objective. Students are first introduced to the design process alongside foundational courses in mathematics, science and engineering, graphic art, design, and aesthetics. They are trained not only in the mechanical aspects of design, but also in electronics, control, and embedded systems, ensuring holistic skill development. The Department offers courses in geometric modelling, finite elements, materials engineering, automotive engineering, mechatronics, robotics, biomedical imaging and diagnostic techniques. heading: 4.9.2. Academic Programmes: MS, PhD and Dual Degree
plain_text: ## 4.9.2. Academic Programmes: MS, PhD and Dual Degree A first of its kind in India, the Department provides much-needed leadership in Engineering Design with two novel dual-degree programmes. Both programmes offer BTech in Engineering Design, and the first programme, that began in 2006, offers MTech in Automotive Engineering. The second programme, launched in 2008, offers MTech in Biomedical Design. Since 2007, the Department has also offered MS and PhD programmes. Two interdisciplinary dual degree programmes in Robotics and Electric Vehicles were started with ED as the coordinating department. The Department also offers research-based MS and PhD programmes.

heading: Equipment Developed
plain_text: ## Equipment Developed Cellular transfection methodologies, which include well-established techniques such as electroporation, microinjection, and sonoporation, encounter inherent limitations that prompt the need for a transformative approach. These limitations revolve around the challenges of achieving uniform intracellular transfection with high efficiency while minimizing cytotoxicity. The imperative for precision in delivery methods becomes especially important in the domains of therapeutic interventions, diagnostics, and drug delivery. Traditional physical techniques like electroporation are scrutinized due to their tendency to result in non-uniform transfection outcomes, exhibit cell specificity, and constrain the throughput of the process. The call for a paradigm shift arises from the awareness that these limitations hinder the full potential of cellular transfection methodologies, necessitating the exploration of alternative strategies to meet the evolving demands of cellular manipulation in biomedical applications. This prototype development introduces an innovative concept termed 'optoporation,' which capitalizes on the combined use of a diode laser and titanium oxide (TiO 2 ) nanostructures. The overarching objective in developing this equipment is to address the inherent deficiencies observed in existing cellular transfection techniques. The research endeavours to establish a novel, costeffective, compact, and versatile intracellular delivery platform tailored for a spectrum of clinical investigations.

heading: EE1: Communications and Signal Processing
plain_text: ## EE1: Communications and Signal Processing Communications and networks: This research group focuses on cutting edge problems in wireless communications and networks, including mathematical modelling, analysis, designing of new algorithms and prototyping using test beds. Their interests span physical-layer aspects, modulation and coding, scheduling and rate adaptation, estimation and detection, resource allocation and optimisation, network control, information theory, 4G/5G technology and standards, LTE systems, MIMO systems, cognitive radios, mobile IP, optical backbone networks and software defined radios and networks. Department of Electrical Engineering <!-- image --> As part of the Institute of Eminence initiative, the following Centres of Excellence and Research Centres have been established in the Department: - Advanced Memory and Computing - Computer Vision - Gallium Nitride Research and Development - Healthcare and Assistive Technologies - Photonic Integrated Circuits - Quantum Information, Communications, and Computing - RF, Analog, and Mixed Signal ICs The collaborative efforts of the Department are currently grouped under the following areas of research: <!-- image --> Image and speech signal processing: This research group's focus is on image processing and computer vision including image deblurring and dehazing, underwater imaging, image and video matting, HDR, face recognition, 3D geometry inpainting and depth from motion blur. They work on developing novel computational cameras and mathematical framework for their analysis as well as deep learning architectures for solving various image processing and computer vision problems. The speech research group works mainly on Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) for Indian languages, deep learning methods for speech recognition and multilingual speech recognition. <!-- image --> A prototype for in-band full duplex radios using offthe-shelf RF components <!-- image --> <!-- image --> 4.10. <!-- image -->

heading: EE3: Microelectronics and MEMS
plain_text: ## EE3: Microelectronics and MEMS The Microelectronics group focuses on design, simulation, modelling, fabrication and testing of micro and nano scale electronic components and systems. The Microelectronics and MEMS Lab in the department is well-equipped for semiconductor device and MEMS fabrication, characterization, modelling and simulation. It has class-100 and class-1000 clean rooms, which house the major facilities that include a mask writer, double-sided lithography facility, substrate bond aligner, LPCVD for polysilicon deposition, PECVD for dielectrics, diffusion furnaces, e-beam metallisation unit and RIE for dry etching. ## EE3: Microelectronics and MEMS The Microelectronics group focuses on design, simulation, modelling, fabrication and testing of micro and nano scale electronic components and systems. The Microelectronics and MEMS Lab in the department is well-equipped for semiconductor device and MEMS fabrication, characterization, modelling and simulation. It has class-100 and class-1000 clean rooms, which house the major facilities that include a mask writer, double-sided lithography facility, substrate bond aligner, LPCVD for polysilicon deposition, PECVD for dielectrics, diffusion furnaces, e-beam metallisation unit and RIE for dry etching. The VLSI group is involved in research in the areas of DSP architectures, FPGAs, mapping of algorithms, and reconfigurable computing. <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image -->

heading: EE5: RF and Photonics
plain_text: ## EE5: RF and Photonics The group focuses on applications in a variety of interdisciplinary areas such as radar systems, satellite imaging, fiber, free-space classical and quantum technologies, optoelectronic devices, lasers, signal processing, metrology and sensing, microwave remote sensing, and microwave imaging. Research activities include design, analysis and synthesis of devices, components, and aspects of system and network design. The group designs, fabricates, and analyses various kinds of silicon photonic, plasmonic and diffractive optic devices. In addition to physical devices, research on Tbps optical communication systems with advanced modulation formats, optical signal processing and quantum communication are also investigated. The group also does active research on discrete and distributed fiber sensors, high-power fiber lasers operating at different wavelengths, narrow-line lasers and pulsed lasers. In the radio or microwave realm, work is ongoing on aspects of satellite remote sensing, inverse microwave imaging, computational electromagnetics, and radio over fiber millimeter wave communications for radar systems, optical fronthauling for 5G networks. There are active research collaborations with several international universities such as the Optoelectronic Research Center Southampton, University of Rochester, University of Melbourne, University of Glasgow, to name a few, and with different Indian industries such as Sterlite Technologies, LightMotif, Forbes Marshall, to name a few. The group receives research funding from different Government agencies, DRDO and industry.

heading: 4.11.1. Introduction
plain_text: ## 4.11.1. Introduction The Department of Humanities and Social Sciences, one of the oldest at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras, has been contributing to the Institute's academic environment since 1959. The Department's essentially inter-disciplinary nature is its distinguishing feature, which allows students to develop an appreciation for a diverse set of fields such as Development Studies, Economics, English Studies, Environmental Studies, Climate Policy, Astronomy, History, International Relations, Philosophy, Cultural Studies and Sociology. The Department offers both Master's and Doctoral programmes, as well as electives for Engineering students. Coupled with its multi-disciplinary background, the Department boasts of a highly diverse and experienced faculty. The Department has an excellent student-teacher ratio, providing opportunities for academically intense learning.

## 4.11.1. Introduction The Department of Humanities and Social Sciences, one of the oldest at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras, has been contributing to the Institute's academic environment since 1959. The Department's essentially inter-disciplinary nature is its distinguishing feature, which allows students to develop an appreciation for a diverse set of fields such as Development Studies, Economics, English Studies, Environmental Studies, Climate Policy, Astronomy, History, International Relations, Philosophy, Cultural Studies and Sociology. The Department offers both Master's and Doctoral programmes, as well as electives for Engineering students. Coupled with its multi-disciplinary background, the Department boasts of a highly diverse and experienced faculty. The Department has an excellent student-teacher ratio, providing opportunities for academically intense learning.

heading: 4.11.2.	 Academic Programmes
plain_text: ## 4.11.2. Academic Programmes Integrated MA (Two-Year Programme) The Department restructured its MA programme in 2022. Instead of a five-year integrated MA, the Department is now offering two-year MA programmes in Development Studies, Economics and English Studies from July 2023. The Department also offers a Dual Degree MA in Public Policy for the Institute's BTech students.

heading: 4.12.2.	 Academic Programmes
plain_text: ## 4.12.2. Academic Programmes The Master of Business Administration (MBA) at DoMS is a two-year full-time programme aimed at training graduates to become capable managers. The programme involves classroom teaching, case discussions, hands-on management internships in industry, and project work. Students are equipped with quantitative tools and techniques necessary for analysing business problems, along with personal skills such as business communication, general business knowledge and interpersonal skills. The coursework is supplemented with industrial training through a summer project for 8-10 weeks after the fourth quarter, along with project work during the seventh quarter. The Executive Programme in Business Administration (EMBA) is designed to equip mid-career working professionals with deep functional and broad industry knowledge, through blended weekend learning. The programme enables working professionals to make strategic investments in their careers while continuing to meet job demands. The Tech MBA programme is part of the five-year interdisciplinary dual-degree programme conceptualised by DoMS. The programme enables undergraduate students of the Institute to engage in a curriculum that integrates and synergises technology and management disciplines. The Tech MBA programme aims to provide knowledge of business functions and strategies, develop expertise in business analytics, and focus on transformation technologies that reshape enterprises, economies, and societies. <!-- image --> Department of Management Studies multi-institutional postgraduate diploma programme (PGPEXVLM) for Visionary Leaders in Manufacturing, along with IIM Calcutta and IIT Kanpur. The major areas of specialisation are - Finance - Human Resource Management and Organisational Behaviour - Information Systems - Marketing - Operations - Strategy DoMS is committed to providing foundational, interdisciplinary, and experiential learning, and a global educational experience to students and industry executives. DoMS prepares individuals to become analytical thinkers and responsible leaders with high standards of professional integrity and ethics. The Quantitative Finance programme is part of the fiveyear interdisciplinary dual-degree programme conceptualised by DoMS. It has a strong interdisciplinary orientation, with faculty participation from the Departments of Mathematics, Computer Science, and Humanities and Social Sciences. The programme enables students to build advanced knowledge in quantitative finance, financial engineering, and risk management, and bridges the gap between the application of modern product and process technologies and state-of-theart finance. The PGPEX-VLM is a unique, one-year full-time residential programme with a built-in manufacturing focus. This programme is conducted jointly by three premier institutes of India: IIM Calcutta, IIT Kanpur, and IIT Madras. The programme introduces courses on green manufacturing, SAP ERP, and breakthrough management, and targets engineers from manufacturing and allied industries. The MS by Research programme is a full-fledged research programme designed for students seeking research-oriented industry roles or wishing to pursue a research career. It is characterised by a significant research component in the curriculum. The flagship PhD or Doctoral programme is a comprehensive research programme designed to develop and provide exceptional faculty resources for management teaching and research. DoMS faculty members are well-accomplished in management research and are recognised for publishing in reputed academic journals. 4.12.

plain_text: ## 4.13.1. Introduction Department of Mathematics <!-- image --> 4.13. The Department of Mathematics was established in 1959 along with the Institute. It offers an MSc programme in Mathematics, an MTech programme in Industrial Mathematics and Scientific Computing (IMSC), and a PhD programme. In addition, the department has taken the responsibility of teaching mathematics courses to BTech, MTech (other than IMSC), MSc and PhD students at the Institute. The major research areas of the department are the following: 1. Algebraic Combinatorics 2. Algebraic Geometry 3. Algebraic Topology 4. Applied Probability 5. Approximation Theory 6. heading: 4.15.1. Introduction
plain_text: ## 4.15.1. Introduction The Department of Medical Sciences and Technology at the Indian Institute of Technology Madras was established in February 2023. The Department aims to set up a world-class research environment for medical sciences and technology in order to develop and train physician scientists and engineering physiologists of the future. By applying engineering principles to medical knowledge, this new class of professionals who transcend medicine and engineering have the potential to revolutionise healthcare delivery both within and outside hospital settings . With a combination of the principles of design, bio-mechanics, electronics technology and the science of ergonomics, powerful medical devices can be developed that enhance the efficacy, safety, and reliability of medical treatments. The Department aims to build a platform for the convergence of engineering teams and medical professionals where products are developed with a clear understanding of the unique needs of patients, how a device might interact with various medical treatments, and pre-existing conditions of the human body. Department of Medical Sciences & Technology <!-- image --> 4.15. With this interdisciplinary approach to improving healthcare outcomes by leveraging engineering and medical knowledge, new technologies can be developed that monitor vital parameters of various organs, detects signs of disease or stress, and provides targeted prevention and treatment options. As engineering and medicine continue to converge, the possibilities are endless. With the right platform and resources, Physician Scientists and Engineering Physiologists will be able to create groundbreaking technology that have a positive impact on patients' lives for generations to come. IITM has entered into Memorandum of Understanding (MoUs) with highly respected medical institutions to begin its PhD Programme and BS in Medical Sciences & Engineering Programme. The affiliated hospitals include Voluntary Health Services, Sankar Nethralaya, MGM Healthcare, Madras Institute of Orthopaedics and Traumatology (MIOT) International, Sri Ramachandra Institute of Higher Education and Research (SRIHER), Madras Medical Mission (MMM) Hospital and Kanchi Kamakoti (KK) CHILDS Trust Hospital.

heading: 4.16.1. Introduction
plain_text: ## 4.16.1. Introduction One of the oldest departments of IIT Madras, the Department of Metallurgical and Materials Engineering (MME), was established in 1959 as the Department of Metallurgy. It was renamed as the Department of Metallurgical and Materials Engineering in 2003. The Department offers BTech, MTech, MS and PhD degree courses, and is actively engaged in research, education, and industrial consultancy. Its teaching, research, and consultancy activities cover a broad spectrum ranging from conventional metallurgy to frontiers of materials science and engineering. The Department is respected for its strong linkages with industry and expertise in industrial metallurgy. Over the years, it has hosted excellent research infrastructure Department of Metallurgical & Materials Engineering <!-- image --> 4.16. in the broad areas of materials science and engineering, such as materials processing (forming, joining, casting, particulate processing and nanostructured materials), characterisation (X-ray diffraction, electron microscopy, and thermal analysis), mechanical testing, corrosion engineering, surface engineering, computational materials science, and electronic materials. The Department continues to strive for excellence and realising its vision of becoming a pioneering Department in the areas of materials science and engineering, while consolidating its strength in traditional areas of metallurgical engineering.

## Advisory Board Members: The initial board members are Mr. MM Murugappan (former chairman of The Murugappa Group, Chennai, India), Dr. Pinakin Chaubal (CTO, Arcelor Mittal Steel, East Chicago, IL, USA, IIT Madras Alumnus of 1978), Prof. Shravan Kumar (Brown University, Providence, Rhode Island, USA, IIT Madras Alumnus of 1979), Dr. C Narayan (IBM Research, San Jose, CA, IIT Madras Alumnus of 1978), Dr. Shubha Kumar (IIT Madras Alumna of 1994, Distinguished Alumnus of 2022). In consultation with the advisory board, the Department Head can appoint additional new members from time to time to maintain reasonable strength of numbers.

plain_text: ## 4.17.1. Introduction The Ministry of Education, as per the decision of the Council of Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), established the Ocean Engineering Centre of IIT Madras in 1977 based on the recommendation of a committee headed by Dr. Y Nayudamma. The department is to act as a Centre of Excellence to advance the frontiers of science, provide breakthrough technology, and develop educational and training programmes in the field of ocean engineering. A national advisory committee monitored the progress of the department over the years. This committee consisted of the representatives of the then Ministry of Education and institutions such as the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), University Grants Commission (UGC), Department of Science & Technology Department of Ocean Engineering <!-- image --> 4.17. (DST), Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC), Engineers India Limited (EIL), other IITs, and user industries, with the Director, IIT Madras as the chairman. A review committee headed by Prof. MGK Menon also reviewed the progress of the department in 1982, and its recommendation has since been implemented towards the department's progress as an independent Centre of Excellence. Ever since, several peer reviews were conducted and their recommendations were implemented. The previous review of the Department was done in 2013. The recommendations of this review have also been implemented by the Department. The latest review was done in 2025.

heading: 4.18.2.	 Academic Programmes
plain_text: ## 4.18.2. Academic Programmes The Department of Physics offers a variety of academic programmes. These include the undergraduate BTech (Engineering Physics) programme, offered in coordination with the Department of Electrical Engineering; three master's programmes, namely the Dual Degree (BS + MS), MSc, and Interdisciplinary Dual Degree (IDDD) in Quantum Science and Technology; MTech programmes in Physics; as well as the regular doctoral research (PhD) programme.

Students from educational institutions, colleges and schools visit the SAIF regularly to gain exposure to the use of sophisticated instruments for analysis.

plain_text: ## 6.1.1. National Programme on Technology Enhanced Learning (NPTEL) The National Programme on Technology Enhanced Learning (NPTEL) is India's largest technical knowledge dissemination and certification programme, involving seven Indian Institutes of Technology. NPTEL is also the largest successfully running multi-institutional project in India. It is a joint initiative by the IITs (Indian Institutes of Technology) and IISc (Indian Institute of Science), and a non-profit consortium supported by the Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India. Its primary goal is to provide quality online education in engineering, basic sciences, humanities, and management. NPTEL offers a vast repository of free video lectures and course materials, which can be accessed by anyone at no cost and without requiring a login. Many courses also offer certification exams, allowing learners to earn a certificate

heading: 6.1.1.1. NPTEL Courses Developed
plain_text: ## 6.1.1.1. NPTEL Courses Developed A variety of web and video-based materials have been developed for courses across several disciplines, including basic sciences, humanities and social sciences, management, and engineering. Since 2003, a total of 3200+ courses have been developed in association with 107 partnering institutes such as IITs, IISc, Indian Institutes of Information Technology (IIITs), Indian Institutes of Science Education and Research (IISERs), the Institute of Mathematical Sciences (IMSc), the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI), and others. NPTEL courses are used extensively by students and faculty members across from the IITs or IISc after successfully completing a course and passing the proctored final exam by paying only a nominal fee for the exam. Throughout the course, the content and assignments are accessible freely. It's a popular platform for students and professionals to enhance their knowledge and skills. (nptel.ac.in) NPTEL was felicitated by the President of India on July 9, 2017 at the National Convention on Digital Initiatives for Higher Education for its commendable contribution to digital initiatives. In 2022, NPTEL won Gold in the Lifelong Learning category of the Wharton-QS Reimagine Education Awards for providing opportunities for personal and professional development, including upskilling and re-skilling. the world to further their knowledge on various subjects. The learning material is supplemented with references and recommended reading material and contains self-assessment quizzes for students. The NPTEL platform has garnered over 1.86 billion combined views across its website and YouTube channel. NPTEL's YouTube channel (youtube.com/iit) stands as the most subscribed educational channel, with 5.3 million+ subscribers and over 81.4 million hours of video content watched. heading: 6.1.1.2. Transcription of NPTEL Video Lectures
plain_text: ## 6.1.1.2. Transcription of NPTEL Video Lectures All NPTEL video lectures are transcribed and edited so that students can access the content of video lectures in the form of textual material (in PDF format) and e-books. The same text is also used for subtitling the video lectures. So far, more than 1,19,472 lectures have been transcribed and more than 99,297 (verified and unverified) videos are available with subtitles in English. The transcript files can be accessed through the URL nptel.ac.in/courses. Since last year, transcription has been carried out using two in-house machine learning (ML) tools, with reviewers editing the transcripts directly within the platform.

heading: Translation of Text Transcripts to Local Languages
plain_text: ## Translation of Text Transcripts to Local Languages To assist and ease the transition of learners who have undergone their schooling in their regional language, NPTEL has initiated the translation of course content into 11 Indian languages, viz. Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Odia, Punjabi, Tamil and Telugu. This endeavour ensures better and effective knowledge transfer and improvement of English skills, as it enables learners to follow along with English-speaking instructors with the help of subtitles in their preferred language. Translated versions of lectures in various languages are available on SWAYAM and NPTEL portal (nptel.ac.in/translation) as PDF transcripts, e-books, subtitles below videos, scrolling text below videos, and in some cases as audio files. A total of 32,270 hours of lectures of 1,464 courses have so far been translated into regional languages.

heading: 6.1.1.11. Utilisation of NPTEL Videos and Web Resources for GATE Prepa
plain_text: ## 6.1.1.11. Utilisation of NPTEL Videos and Web Resources for GATE Preparation NPTEL, recognising the importance of the Graduate Aptitude Test in Engineering (GATE) for postgraduate admissions and public sector undertaking (PSU) recruitment, has developed a dedicated GATE preparation portal with corporate social responsibility (CSR) support from Amadeus Labs, Bengaluru. This platform aligns the GATE syllabus across 13 engineering disciplines with NPTEL's rich video course content, helping reduce dependence on private coaching. Over 1 lakh students have registered on the portal, and more than 2,000 live mentoring sessions have been conducted to support aspirants. In addition to the portal, the NPTEL GATE Preparation YouTube channel offers over 550 hours of content across 5,000+ videos and has a subscriber base of 16.2K. A comprehensive question bank with over 1,000 questions per subject has been developed for biotechnology, chemistry, civil engineering, computer science and information technology, electrical engineering, electronics and communication engineering, mechanical engineering, physics, mathematics, and life sciences, along with the conduction of 165+ mock tests. These resources are available at gate.nptel.ac.in.

heading: 6.1.2.2. IITM BS in Electronic Systems
plain_text: ## 6.1.2.2. IITM BS in Electronic Systems The BS Degree in Electronic Systems is a four-year hybrid undergraduate programme offered by IIT Madras, designed to provide a strong foundation in electronics, embedded systems, and hardware design. Open to students who have completed Class 12 who have studied mathematics and physics, the programme aims to build industry-ready professionals with hands-on skills in circuits, embedded programming, signal processing, and systems integration. The course structure includes Foundation, Diploma, and BS-level content. With a flexible learning model, proctored exams across India, and multiple exit options, this programme allows learners to earn a certificate, diploma, or BS degree while studying at their own pace. <!-- image --> The highlight of the programme is that all labs are conducted in person at IIT Madras, for which students have to travel to IITM for 3-4 days at the end of the term. There are five such labs at the Foundation Level and four labs to be completed at the Diploma Level. <!-- image --> Glimpses of students at the lab <!-- image -->

heading: 6.2.1. Introduction
plain_text: ## 6.2.1. Introduction The Office of Industrial Consultancy and Sponsored Research (IC&SR) at IIT Madras was set up in 1973 to foster and promote funded research activities as well as relationships with industries and other organisations both from India and abroad. The IC&SR facilitates faculty members' active participation in various interactive programmes organised for the benefit of industries and the Institute. It also plays a proactive role in providing legal support for memoranda of understanding (MoUs) with funding agencies and intellectual property (IP) protection and commercialisation. In addition, it provides administrative support for carrying out sponsored research projects and consultancy assignments, procurements (equipment & others) for projects, project staff recruitment and related establishment activities, maintenance of accounts, and funding agencies' compliance such as issuing of Utilisation Certificates (UCs) and statements of account, Goods & Services Tax (GST), tax deducted at source (TDS), etc. Some of the major activities of the centre are: - Sponsored research programmes - Consultancy projects: research-based, retainer, and institutional projects - Collaborative projects with organisations and industries in India and foreign countries - Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)-IITM Space Technology Cell projects and other Cell/focused centre projects - IP protection (patenting) and technology transfer (TT) - Faculty and student entrepreneurship and incubation - Common research facilities: procurement, installation and access to users through the Equipment Reservation System (ERS) portal - Facilitation of international research collaborations - Centres of Excellence (CoEs) in frontier areas - Facilitation of industry-Institute research interactions - Outreach: organising research and development (R&D) events; participating in R&D events organised by others; communicating R&D activities through print & social media - Faculty research enhancement: new faculty initiation and seed grants (NFIG and NFSG), exploratory research, support for sustaining research, Institute Research and Development Award (IRDA), funding for maintenance of equipment - Participating in various national R&D and intellectual property awards competitions

heading: 6.2.5.2. Major Research Projects Undertaken
plain_text: ## 6.2.5.2. Major Research Projects Undertaken - The Department of Science and Technology, Government of India, under the National Supercomputing Mission, sanctioned a project titled 'Shakti SoC test tapeout with 64-bit Out of Order (OoO) core and AI/ML (artificial intelligence/machine learning) accelerator', with a sanction value of INR 30.86 crore for 9 months, starting from May 2025. This project aims to develop high-performance computing platforms for general-purpose and AI/ML applications. - The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology has sanctioned a project titled 'Integrated Surgical Platform with Navigation, Robot, Simulation & Training for Total Knee Arthroplasty', with a sanction value of INR 25.08 crore for a period of 4.5 years. This is a collaborative project with other organisations, and aims to develop an integrated total knee arthroplasty suite for knee joint replacement surgery assisted through navigation robotics in a surgical environment and a VR/AR/MR/XR (virtual, augmented, mixed and extended reality) platform for surgical simulation & training. - The Ministry of Earth Sciences has funded a project titled 'AUV (autonomous underwater vehicle) development along with a homing and docking station' with a sanction value of INR 11.70 crore for a period of one year under the Deep Ocean Mission scheme. This project aims to design and develop a homing and docking system including AUV navigation for underwater docking. - National Technical Research Organisation has funded a project titled 'Demodulation of Complex Waveforms', with a sanction value of INR ~10.52 crore, for a period of one year. This project aims to develop a solution to address online demodulation of complex waveforms (carrier-in-carrier) along with an intelligent waveform library. - The Department of Science and Technology has funded INR 5.57 crore to augment the research infrastructure at the Chemistry Department under the Fund for Improvement of Science & Technology Infrastructure (FIST) 2024 for over a period of five years. ESR (electron spin resonance), XPS-UPS (X-ray photoelectron spectrometer-ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy) and AFM (atomic force microscope) equipment will be procured using this fund. - The Ministry of Education, through the Scheme for Promotion of Academic and Research Collaboration (SPARC), has funded INR 5.65 crore for nine projects over two years to carry out research along with international research collaborators in the areas of aerospace, applied mechanics, chemical, electrical, and mechanical engineering. - The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has funded the Shri S Ramakrishnan Centre of Excellence for Research in Fluid and Thermal Sciences for a period of five years to carry out research in the areas of fluid and thermal sciences. This centre was inaugurated by Dr. V Narayanan, Chairman, ISRO on March 17, 2025 in the presence of Dr. V Kamakoti, Director, IIT Madras. The ISRO has funded INR 1.84 crores towards this Centre's activities during the current financial year. <!-- image --> - Hyundai Motor India Limited and Guidance Tamil Nadu established the Hydrogen Valley Innovation Hub as a technical R&D Centre at the IIT Madras Discovery Campus, Thaiyur. This centre aims to create an ecosystem of localisation of electrolyser/fuel cell manufacturing and create a green hydrogen-related curriculum for skill development. Hyundai Motor has sanctioned INR 100 crore for these aims over a period of five years. - The Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corporation Ltd. (HSBC) has funded INR 21.26 crore over a period of five years towards a centre for resource efficiency, recyclability and circularity in energy transition. This centre aims to carry out transformational, fundamental research and technology translation to achieve global net zero goals in terms of battery waste.

Major Research Projects Undertaken - The Department of Science and Technology, Government of India, under the National Supercomputing Mission, sanctioned a project titled 'Shakti SoC test tapeout with 64-bit Out of Order (OoO) core and AI/ML (artificial intelligence/machine learning) accelerator', with a sanction value of INR 30.86 crore for 9 months, starting from May 2025. This project aims to develop high-performance computing platforms for general-purpose and AI/ML applications. - The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology has sanctioned a project titled 'Integrated Surgical Platform with Navigation, Robot, Simulation & Training for Total Knee Arthroplasty', with a sanction value of INR 25.08 crore for a period of 4.5 years. This is a collaborative project with other organisations, and aims to develop an integrated total knee arthroplasty suite for knee joint replacement surgery assisted through navigation robotics in a surgical environment and a VR/AR/MR/XR (virtual, augmented, mixed and extended reality) platform for surgical simulation & training. - The Ministry of Earth Sciences has funded a project titled 'AUV (autonomous underwater vehicle) development along with a homing and docking station' with a sanction value of INR 11.70 crore for a period of one year under the Deep Ocean Mission scheme. This project aims to design and develop a homing and docking system including AUV navigation for underwater docking. - National Technical Research Organisation has funded a project titled 'Demodulation of Complex Waveforms', with a sanction value of INR ~10.52 crore, for a period of one year. This project aims to develop a solution to address online demodulation of complex waveforms (carrier-in-carrier) along with an intelligent waveform library. - The Department of Science and Technology has funded INR 5.57 crore to augment the research infrastructure at the Chemistry Department under the Fund for Improvement of Science & Technology Infrastructure (FIST) 2024 for over a period of five years. ESR (electron spin resonance), XPS-UPS (X-ray photoelectron spectrometer-ultraviolet photoelectron spectroscopy) and AFM (atomic force microscope) equipment will be procured using this fund. - The Ministry of Education, through the Scheme for Promotion of Academic and Research Collaboration (SPARC), has funded INR 5.65 crore for nine projects over two years to carry out research along with international research collaborators in the areas of aerospace, applied mechanics, chemical, electrical, and mechanical engineering. - The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has funded the Shri S Ramakrishnan Centre of Excellence for Research in Fluid and Thermal Sciences for a period of five years to carry out research in the areas of fluid and thermal sciences. This centre was inaugurated by Dr. V Narayanan, Chairman, ISRO on March 17, 2025 in the presence of Dr. V Kamakoti, Director, IIT Madras. The ISRO has funded INR 1.84 crores towards this Centre's activities during the current financial year. <!-- image --> - Hyundai Motor India Limited and Guidance Tamil Nadu established the Hydrogen Valley Innovation Hub as a technical R&D Centre at the IIT Madras Discovery Campus, Thaiyur. This centre aims to create an ecosystem of localisation of electrolyser/fuel cell manufacturing and create a green hydrogen-related curriculum for skill development. Hyundai Motor has sanctioned INR 100 crore for these aims over a period of five years. - The Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corporation Ltd. (HSBC) has funded INR 21.26 crore over a period of five years towards a centre for resource efficiency, recyclability and circularity in energy transition. This centre aims to carry out transformational, fundamental research and technology translation to achieve global net zero goals in terms of battery waste.

heading: 6.2.17. Research Fund
plain_text: ## 6.2.17. Research Fund To promote research activities at IIT Madras, the Board of IC&SR decided to use its corpus to support several new initiatives. A part of the IC&SR Office's earnings from consultancy projects was invested in term deposits, and the interest earned through them is used to support schemes such as exploratory research projects (ERP), New Faculty Initiation Grant (NFIG), R&D Award and IP Cell activities. The broad expense allocations for this financial year are given below: - a) R&D Award: The IC&SR Office provides 50% of the award money from its Research Fund to the awardees of the Institute Research & Development Awards. A total of INR 65 lakh was provided to four awardees from IC&SR funds. - b) Exploratory Research Projects: This initiative is to support projects from faculty members who have breakthrough ideas and wish to initiate work without waiting for their proposals to be sanctioned by the funding agency. Under this scheme, a maximum of INR 10 lakh is given for a 12-month period. 26 projects were sanctioned during the financial year 2024-25 with a total value of INR 203.79 lakh . - c) New Faculty Initiation Grant: This is a start-up grant up given to new faculty members, with a maximum amount of INR 5 lakh. During FY 2024-25, 30 faculty members were funded through the Research Fund and 12 other faculty members were funded through various alumni funding. - d) Patenting and Commercialisation Activities by IP Cell: A maximum amount of INR 50 lakh is earmarked per year for these activities. - e) Maintenance of Capital Equipment and Operation of Research Facilities: Under the Research Funds for Maintenance of Equipment (RFME) scheme, the IC&SR Office supports the maintenance and operation of major (costing INR 30 lakh & above) research equipment. This support extends to one year's worth of annual maintenance charges, hiring a technical person, and consumables (in special cases, 50%) for maintaining and operating selected research facilities that can be made available to faculty members and students of the Institute (other than the facility's home department) for at least four hours per day or 20 hours per week. Budget support is normally a maximum of INR 8 lakh per faculty. To avail funds under this scheme, equipment booking should be enabled through the Equipment Reservation System (ERS) portal of the Institute, i.e. https://ers.iitm.ac.in/webroot/home.php. During FY 2024-25, funds for 17 facilities were sanctioned, with a total amount of INR 72.62 lakh, under the RFME scheme.

During FY 2024-25, 30 faculty members were funded through the Research Fund and 12 other faculty members were funded through various alumni funding. - d) Patenting and Commercialisation Activities by IP Cell: A maximum amount of INR 50 lakh is earmarked per year for these activities. - e) Maintenance of Capital Equipment and Operation of Research Facilities: Under the Research Funds for Maintenance of Equipment (RFME) scheme, the IC&SR Office supports the maintenance and operation of major (costing INR 30 lakh & above) research equipment. This support extends to one year's worth of annual maintenance charges, hiring a technical person, and consumables (in special cases, 50%) for maintaining and operating selected research facilities that can be made available to faculty members and students of the Institute (other than the facility's home department) for at least four hours per day or 20 hours per week. Budget support is normally a maximum of INR 8 lakh per faculty. To avail funds under this scheme, equipment booking should be enabled through the Equipment Reservation System (ERS) portal of the Institute, i.e. https://ers.iitm.ac.in/webroot/home.php. During FY 2024-25, funds for 17 facilities were sanctioned, with a total amount of INR 72.62 lakh, under the RFME scheme.

The workshop was conducted by Mr. G Padmanabhan (Vice President, Thermal Division) and his team from LCGC BioAnalytic Solutions. <!-- image -->

heading: (c) IInvenTiv 2025
plain_text: ## (c) IInvenTiv 2025 The IC&SR Office organised IInvenTiv 2025, the 3rd edition of the R&D Innovation Fair of Higher Education Institutes of India at IC&SR, IIT Madras on February 28 and March 1, 2025. It is an initiative of the Ministry of Education. IInvenTiv 2025 is the R&D fair where all IITs, NITs, IISERs, IIITs and other top 50 institutions (in the NIRF 2024 Engineering category) come together to showcase their R&D activity. It serves as a platform for showcasing cutting-edge research and fostering collaboration between academia and industry. 42 NIRF topranked institutions participated in this R&D fair. The Union Education Minister Shri Dharmendra Pradhan attended the event virtually. The event was inaugurated by Dr. Sukanta Majumdar, the Minister of State for Education, Government of India in the presence of Prof. V Kamakoti, Director, IIT Madras, Prof. Manu Santhanam, Dean (IC&SR) and Prof. R Sarathi, Dean (Planning). Dr. Majumdar released a coffee table book titled Prabhav-From Ideas to Impact on leading technological innovations from Indian higher education institutions, which have led to great impacts on the industry. The exhibit catalogue and a coffee table book on one year of SWAYAM (Study Webs of Active-Learning for <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> Young Aspiring Minds) Plus was also released on the occasion. The Minister also felicitated the Yuvamanthan Hackathon winners from participating institutions. During the event, several MoUs were signed with industry partners for technology transfer and research collaborations. <!-- image --> 'Chintan Shivir' or Brainstorming Sessions were conducted over the course of IInvenTiv 2025 in different thematic areas, each featuring experts from government, industry, academia, and startups. The thematic areas that were covered included Circularity and Sustainability (Energy and E-Mobility), Medical/Healthcare Engineering, Aviation Defence and Space, Marine Technologies, AI/ML Technologies, Smart Cities and Infrastructure, Advanced Manufacturing (Industry 4.0+/5.0), and Rural Technologies. <!-- image --> Closed-door Roundtable Discussion: Mr. Madhav Narayan, CEO of IIT Madras Global Research Foundation, led the roundtable discussion that took place between Dr. Sukanta Majumdar, Hon'ble Minister of State for Education, and leaders (from both India & abroad) of industry, venture capitalists, angel investors, academic institutions, army and ISRO, and consul generals of foreign countries. It discussed the current issues in conducting highend research and technology transfer to industry and others, government initiatives to further these activities, and ways to expand these activities moving forward. <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> R&D Expo Stalls: As part of this event, over 140 research exhibits (of types: technology development & transfer, high-end R&D, and startups) from 37 premier institutions were exhibited. The IIT Madras pavilion showcased R&D activities in various CoEs, departments, and the IITM Incubation Cell and Research Park, apart from IP management and TT activities in the Institute. At the valedictory function, Prof. Manu Santhanam, Dean (IC&SR), gave a detailed summary of the fair, presenting insights into the innovative projects exhibited, panel discussions, and collaborations initiated during the event. Dr. Nagahanumaiah, Director, Central Manufacturing Technology Institute, Bengaluru was the chief guest for the function, and emphasised the <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> importance of R&D in driving technological progress. This was followed by an inspiring speech by Prof. Kamakoti, who also shared insights from these fairs and encouraged young minds to persist in their research endeavours. Rapporteurs gave a brief summary of each topic discussed under the Chintan Shivir sessions. A special vote of thanks was delivered by Dr. V Arumugam, Chief Manager (Technical), IC&SR, who was part of the local organising committee. He expressed gratitude to the steering committee, all participants, and exhibitors from various institutes, who contributed to the fair's success. A large number of visitors from industry, government functionaries, foreign country representatives, faculty members, students and media persons from throughout India & abroad visited the R&D stalls and attended the technical sessions.

heading: Modernisation/Upgradation of Handlooms at Weaving Centres
plain_text: ## Modernisation/Upgradation of Handlooms at Weaving Centres RuTAG IIT Madras is collaborating with the Kerala State Handloom Directorate to upgrade technology in handloom production centres and address inefficiencies caused by manual labour-intensive processes. With nearly 25,000 handlooms in operation, most of which are locally fabricated with non-standardised parts, the sector requires technological interventions to improve productivity, reduce drudgery, and enhance operational efficiency. To facilitate this initiative, a memorandum of understanding (MoU) has been signed, with Prof. Shankar Krishna Pillai as the Principal Project Coordinator. The anticipated improvements in productivity and efficiency will lead to higher wages and encourage greater youth participation in the handloom sector.

heading: Field Survey on Khadi Spinning and Weaving
plain_text: ## Field Survey on Khadi Spinning and Weaving RuTAG IIT Madras, in collaboration with Prof. Manish Anand and the Khadi and Village Industries Board (KKVIB), conducted a detailed assessment of Khadi spinning and weaving centres in Palakkad and Thrissur, Kerala. The field survey covered 400 artisans and revealed that around 30% of spinning <!-- image --> <!-- image --> charkas and 15% of weaving looms were non-functional, affecting productivity. The spinning machinery observed used an 8-spindle system with gear and belt-pulley drives. While the gear train was mostly efficient, the belt drive showed slack, causing inefficient power transmission and inconsistencies in yarn quality due to non-uniform handle movement. The weaving machines also demanded significant manual input, including manual shuttle movement and dual pedal operation, increasing user fatigue and reducing output quality. Based on the survey findings and technical observations, RuTAG initiated the Next-Generation Spinning Machine Project. This aims to redesign existing equipment with improved ergonomic features and integrate digital monitoring to enhance performance, worker safety, and comfort. The modernisation effort is directed at improving the quality and efficiency of khadi production while promoting sustainable livelihoods for rural artisans. <!-- image --> <!-- image -->

heading: 10 // Dissemination of Electronic Jacquard Handloom, West Bengal, Medi
plain_text: ## 10 // Dissemination of Electronic Jacquard Handloom, West Bengal, Medinipur RuTAG IIT Madras is actively engaged in the dissemination of the 384-hook electronic Jacquard handloom (EJH) technology for weaving superfine Madur mats and Masland mats among grass mat weavers in Medinipur, West Bengal. This initiative, undertaken in collaboration with the West Bengal Khadi and Village Industries Board <!-- image --> <!-- image --> (WBKVIB) and Jadavpur University, aims to modernise traditional handloom practices and enhance artisan livelihoods. The EJH prototype was successfully tested using locally sourced Madur grass, demonstrating improved weaving efficiency, reduced manual effort, and enhanced product quality. As part of the dissemination process, RuTAG completed all preparatory work, identified a suitable fabricator, and conducted a field visit to Medinipur, where two beneficiaries were selected and validated with the assistance of WBKVIB and Jadavpur University. The beneficiaries have been requested to complete necessary civil and building works to enable the erection of the EJH units. The initiative is currently in progress, with future plans for wider implementation across multiple weaving communities to promote sustainable livelihoods and encourage youth engagement in the sector.

heading: 11 // HPDS Mini Dryer & AI-Based Moisture Detection
plain_text: ## 11 // HPDS Mini Dryer & AI-Based Moisture Detection RuTAG IIT Madras is developing an HPDS Mini Dryer to enhance energy-efficient drying solutions for small-scale farmers. The dryer is designed to reduce energy consumption by 30%, improve drying speed, and preserve product quality. Unlike conventional dryers, it incorporates advanced electronic controllers for precise drying process optimisation. AI integration is being explored using a YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once version 8)-based deep learning model for real-time moisture detection in crops like cardamom. The AIdriven system classifies moisture levels, enabling automated monitoring and improved drying efficiency. Performance evaluations are <!-- image --> <!-- image --> underway to refine the design, optimise energy efficiency, and enhance process repeatability. This initiative aims to reduce manual intervention, enhance consistency, and boost productivity, thereby promoting sustainable agricultural practices and strengthening rural economic empowerment. <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image -->

heading: 2. Workshops
plain_text: ## 2. Workshops - During FY 2024-25, the IPM Cell delivered 16 presentations with respect to IP to various internal and external researchers and entrepreneurs. - As part of the FY 2024-25 agenda, the IPM Cell successfully organised the 'Have an Idea (HAI) Programme-Idea to Asset' on two occasions: September 18, 2024 and January 30, 2025. The sessions brought faculty members, research scholars, and student inventors to brainstorm and refine their ideas prior to submitting the Invention Disclosure Form (IDF). The programme included insightful discussions on the basics of intellectual property rights (IPR), a demonstration of patentability searches, and an overview of the patent filing process and internal process flow. heading: 3. Search and Techno-Commercial Evaluations
plain_text: ## 3. Search and Techno-Commercial Evaluations - The IPM Cell has an efficient in-house search team for performing prior art searches across different technology domains before filing patent applications, which resulted in reducing the attorney costs for external searches. - The in-house IP search team currently utilises three paid databases-Questel Orbit, PatSeer, and the AI-based tool XLSCOUT-to conduct effective prior art searches. Notably, students have unlimited access to XLSCOUT through their LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) credentials via the Institute's library. Additionally, PatSeer Explorer, a user-friendly tool designed for inventors, has been introduced to further support and simplify prior art search activities in 2024-25. - The IPM Cell provides constant support and guidance to inventors for performing Level 1 pre-IDF searches using the above-mentioned databases through discussions. - The IPM in-house search team conducted patentability searches for about 241 inventions for Indian filing. The IPM Cell also coordinated with empanelled attorneys for about 96 external patentability searches in FY 2024-25. - The IPM Cell performed novelty checks and provided reports for over 34 IITM Pravartak proposals. - The IPM Cell facilitated in-house provisional patent filing of seven applications through the e-filing portal of the Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks, Government of India, thereby ensuring the novelty of all inventions by filing provisional patents before the inventions' publication, and retained the priority of these applications. - The techno-commercial evaluations (TCE) to assess the IP and commercial potential of 50 inventions were carried out by a third party (KPMG). These reports encompass an analysis of specifications and ranking scales for technical, business, and strategic factors, as well as commercial viability. They also provide an overall potential rating for the inventions and recommend jurisdictions for PCT/foreign filings.

heading: 6.3.1. Introduction
plain_text: ## 6.3.1. Introduction The Central Electronics Centre (CEC) was established in 1971 with the main objective of servicing and maintaining the wide variety of sophisticated electronic equipment at the Institute. A key attribute of this centre is its blend of an academic environment and an industry-like working atmosphere. The Centre is housed in a dust-free environment. It has a team of qualified, experienced and talented staff members, trained in India and Germany in various aspects of electronic instrumentation, testing and calibration. The infrastructural facilities and equipment have been continually enhanced over the years using Government of India (GOI) funds and successive Indo-German collaborative projects. When the Centre was established in 1971, a critical need for training service engineers for maintaining electronic equipment was foreseen, and an 18-month training programme, the first of its kind in the country, was started in the same year. The period of the training programme was later extended to 24 months. In view of the large demand for trained personnel both within and outside the Institute, conducting such long-term training programmes has become one of the important activities of the CEC. The Centre has diversified its activities and now offers the following services: - Servicing and maintenance of electronic equipment/instruments - Offering one-year training programmes for manpower development - Conducting Electronics module workshop for first-year BTech students

## 6.3.1. Introduction The Central Electronics Centre (CEC) was established in 1971 with the main objective of servicing and maintaining the wide variety of sophisticated electronic equipment at the Institute. A key attribute of this centre is its blend of an academic environment and an industry-like working atmosphere. The Centre is housed in a dust-free environment. It has a team of qualified, experienced and talented staff members, trained in India and Germany in various aspects of electronic instrumentation, testing and calibration. The infrastructural facilities and equipment have been continually enhanced over the years using Government of India (GOI) funds and successive Indo-German collaborative projects. When the Centre was established in 1971, a critical need for training service engineers for maintaining electronic equipment was foreseen, and an 18-month training programme, the first of its kind in the country, was started in the same year. The period of the training programme was later extended to 24 months. In view of the large demand for trained personnel both within and outside the Institute, conducting such long-term training programmes has become one of the important activities of the CEC. The Centre has diversified its activities and now offers the following services: - Servicing and maintenance of electronic equipment/instruments - Offering one-year training programmes for manpower development - Conducting Electronics module workshop for first-year BTech students

heading: 6.4.1. Introduction
plain_text: ## 6.4.1. Introduction The Computer Centre at IIT Madras was established in 1973 to provide centralised computing resources and support to the academic initiatives of the Institute. It has had a number of professionally-maintained facilities that have served the IIT Madras community-from the International Business Machines (IBM) System/370 in the 1970s and the Siemens system in the 1980s, to the Silicon Graphics Inc. (SGI), IBM Power and Sun systems in the earlier part of this millennium, and the supercomputers and communication and network services of today. Over the years, the computing and information technology requirements of the IIT Madras community have increased. The Computer Centre's organisation has evolved with this increase in requirements. In 2007, the infrastructure of the Centre was significantly upgraded through an endowment given by S Gopalakrishnan in the name of his father PG Senapathy. The activities of the Centre are organised under five verticals: 1. High-Performance Computing Environment (HPCE), 2. E-Services, 3. Network, 4. Data Centre, and 5. Workflow. Each vertical is focused on continually improving its services to meet the needs of the IIT Madras community. The Computer Centre has been International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 9000 certified since 1999. The Technischer Überwachungsverein (TUV) has certified the Computer Centre as an ISO 9001:2015 standard management system for a period of three years, from August 2020 to August 2023, after conducting the final auditing as per TUV NORD <!-- image --> CERT procedures. Currently, it maintains all its processes in conformance with ISO 9001:2015 standards and is certified along with other units at the Institute by TUV NORD. This section presents the background of each vertical and a summary of its annual activities. PG Senapathy Centre for Computing Resources 6.4. <!-- image -->

heading: Aqua Cluster
plain_text: ## Aqua Cluster A supercomputing cluster named Aqua has been operational for the last four years at the HPCE. The racks are based on a water-cooled system, populated with 280 central processing unit (CPU) nodes and 15 graphics processing unit (GPU) nodes, a 1 petabyte (PB) parallel system, and 200 terabytes (TB) of storage in the network-attached storage (NAS) file system. The following are some active research areas that use the Aqua cluster: aerospace engineering, atmospheric and ocean modelling, analysis of large structures, flows and combustion modelling, atomistic simulations, computational material sciences, social, ecological and physical network modelling, numerical weather prediction and data assimilation, microstructure simulation, molecular modelling, spectroscopy, and very-large-scale integration (VLSI). This machine, which caters to the needs of the research community, mostly uses parallel programming. The detailed system configuration is as below:

heading: PARAM Shakti Supercomputing Facility
plain_text: ## PARAM Shakti Supercomputing Facility The PARAM Rudra Supercomputing Facility at IIT Madras along with the Infrastructure supporting it, named PARAM Shakti, represents a significant advancement in computing power and infrastructure. A new cluster called PARAM Shakti, a 3.1 peta floating-point operations per second (PFLOPS) supercomputing system, has been added to the HPCE. This system is primarily based on a water-cooled architecture, enhancing its energy efficiency and performance. PARAM Shakti is a high-performance supercomputer developed under the National Supercomputing Mission (NSM). It is built on PARAM Rudra servers, a powerful computing platform designed to perform complex calculations and simulations with exceptional speed and scalability. The supercomputer features a heterogeneous and hybrid architecture, combining Intel Xeon 2nd Gen Cascade Lake processors with Nvidia Ampere A100 GPUs. The system was designed and implemented by the High Performance Computing (HPC) Technologies Group at the Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (C-DAC). <!-- image --> <!-- image -->
