heading: 6.4.4. Network
plain_text: ## 6.4.4. Network The campus computer network was established in 1994, connecting about 18 buildings in the Academic Zone using telephone cables. The initial bandwidth was 64 kilobytes per second (kBps). Today, we have a fibre-backbone high-speed network connectivity of 10 Gbps for all the buildings in the Academic Zone. In addition, a backbone inter-connecting the three zones (Academic Zone, Hostel Zone and Residential Zone) is also operational. The total number of nodes in the Campus is approximately 25,000. The network equipment in the Academic Zone was upgraded to provide 100/1000 megabytes per second (MBps) connectivity to the nodes. All the buildings in the Academic Zone are provided with dual fibre connectivity. Facilities for video conferencing, virtual classrooms, webcasting important events, Eduroam and virtual private network (VPN) are also provided under the network service. The Network vertical also oversees the procurement of external network services, as well as the design, installation and maintenance of the network structure, switches and cabling across the Institute campus.

heading: New Virtualisation Setup
plain_text: ## New Virtualisation Setup VMware powers multi-cloud strategy with leading public cloud providers offering hybrid-compatible services based on the same VMware Cloud stack, including Google Cloud VMware Engine, IBM Cloud for VMware Solutions, Microsoft Azure VMware Solution, and Oracle Cloud VMware Solution. And over 200 VMware cloud provider programme partners offer VMware Cloud verified hybrid cloud services on the same VMware Cloud stack. VMware Cloud Foundation delivers enterprise agility, reliability, and efficiency seeking a private, hybrid, or multicloud solution, with a single dashboard that can manage both virtual machines on premises, on cloud, migration of virtual machines and vice versa. The procured solution, HCI-VMware VSan Refresh and Migration, has a hardware warranty for 5 years with two installations, viz., Data Center (DC) and Disaster Recovery (DR). The DC installation consists of: Three Dell PowerEdge R760 servers, 144 cores, 230 TB of storage and 2TB memory. The DR installation proposed at Thaiyur campus consists of: Three Dell PowerEdge R760 servers, 144 cores, 230 TB storage, 2 TB memory, Smart Rack, and a backup server. Software support for 3 years of VMware Cloud Foundation, VMware vSAN, VMware live, and recovery from Veeam Backup are included. The E-Services team has taken up vulnerability assessment and penetration testing (VAPT) for 25 websites of the Institute and will expand this to cover most of the public-facing websites. To ease peer communication among students, E-Services has installed Discourse, an open-source platform for community discussion. <!-- image --> Academic Activities and Remote Access: During the year, academic activities such as admission tests, online classes, and seminars were successfully conducted using various web-conferencing platforms. Additionally, online course registration was done over the internet, allowing students to complete the process remotely from their homes. VPN services facilitated secure remote access to the Institute's computing resources for students, faculty, and staff. Network and Connectivity: The Computer Centre manages the entire Campus network infrastructure, which includes approximately 30,000 wired nodes spread across departments, hostels, residences, and common facilities. Local area network (LAN) and wireless connectivity is available and authenticated via IITM-LDAP covering academic buildings, research labs, classrooms, seminar halls, and outdoor areas.

heading: 6.4.6. Workflow
plain_text: ## 6.4.6. Workflow The implementation of enterprise resource planning (ERP) software, or what is internally referred to as Workflow, is done by the Workflow group at the Computer Centre. The group works with various sections in the Institute to support system usage and capture changes in requirements involved in process development activities, maintaining reporting websites that collect data from Workflow, and generating reports using new software tools. Online processes have the distinct advantages of transparency, accessibility, and analytics.. Processes such as the Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) payment gateway, No Objection Certificate (NOC) process creation, examiner honorariums, obtaining provisional certificates, linear grade card for the online MTech programme, grade card to storage, all faculty levels' access to Workflow, etc. were introduced. All these processes have a tracking system, which is Task Summary. The Task Summary screen has been enhanced. The reports are flexible and data can be searched with ease. Like optimised processes, there are SLAs (Service Level Agreements) implemented at various steps of the process to move them automatically to avoid delays in completing the processes, and automatic e-mail triggers for each process. Enhancements to the synopsis and thesis evaluation process were carried out. A new A5 thesis process has been introduced for scholars. Along with regular development and optimisation activities, a new portal for web-enabled programmes such as online MTech and MBA has been created, and a trial run was carried out in this financial year. This portal enabled the management to design the curriculum for new programmes in flexible periods instead of a rigid semester or quarter system. Moodle support is handled by the Workflow team. As soon as the Student Electives Allocation Tool (SEAT) allocation for electives gets completed, the courses are moved to Workflow and then to Moodle. Similarly, immediately after the course add/drop week, the courses are updated in Moodle. All the Moodle service requests, managing the Moodle server, and the security of the same are taken care of by the Workflow team. Like in the previous financial year, the data extracted from Workflow has been analysed and utilised by the Administration to align our internal processes to support our vision for IIT Madras. During this financial year, the Workflow team has coordinated the development of a Hospital Management Information System (HMIS) for the Institute Hospital, a visitor management system (VMS) for the Institute security, a new academic portal for the academic section, a renewed Faculty Application Portal (FAP) for the faculty and an augmented Workflow reports site.

heading: 6.5.1.1.	 Introduction
plain_text: ## 6.5.1.1. Introduction The Central Skill Training and Fabrication Facility (CSTF), formerly known as the Central Workshop (CWS), was established in the year 1959 as part of the Department of Mechanical Engineering, with the support of the Federal Republic of Germany, to train BTech students of the Institute in various shop floor techniques and fabrications. The CSTF is now an academic facility of IIT Madras and has International Standard Organization (ISO) 9001:2015 quality certification. The core activities of the CSTF are to offer hands-on training to BTech/Dual Degree students and to support the fabrication works of students and research scholars of various departments of the Institute. The practical training offered by the CSTF is part of academic curriculum requirement of BTech/ Dual Degree students. The CSTF offers the following course codes: WS1031, WS1032 and WS1303. The CSTF's facilities are modernised from time to time based on technological needs for skill training and fabrication.

heading: 6.5.2. Central Glass Blowing Section
plain_text: ## 6.5.2. Central Glass Blowing Section Established in 1971, the Central Glass Blowing Section (CGBS) is one of the important infrastructural facilities of Indian Institute of Technology Madras. The facility undertakes design and fabrication of sophisticated glass apparatus for research and development in various departments. It has a range of modern glass working equipment that has been largely procured from Germany under a collaborative programme. The apparatus includes a horizontal-cum-vertical lathe, a universal forming lathe and a high-vacuum system. The Section is also well equipped with a good number of sophisticated burners, drilling and cutting machines, grinding and polishing equipment and other such tools necessary for fashioning varied glass apparatus. It has an adequate facility for quartz working and has developed a high level of expertise in this area. The sophisticated apparatus fabricated includes cryostats, spherical and cylindrical Dewar flasks, lugging probes, laser housing tubes with water jackets, reactor tubes, vacuum tube collectors (for solar energy) and quartz ware. Central Glass Blowing Section 6.5.2. The Section undertook 617 work orders from various departments between April 1, 2024 and March 31, 2025.

plain_text: ## 7.1.1 Introduction 7. Our alumni community and corporate partners continue to be the cornerstone of IIT Madras' journey towards global excellence. Over the years, our alumni have championed the Institute's growth-establishing advanced research centres, supporting key infrastructure, and endowing scholarships that empower future generations. Equally transformative is our strong industryacademia collaboration, enabled through Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiatives driven by our valued corporate partners. At the heart of these efforts is the Office of Alumni and Corporate Relations (A&CR), serving as the vital link that unites these two powerful entities with IIT Madras. Through strategic outreach and fundraising, the A&CR Office strives to create an ecosystem comprising the alumni community, industry leaders, entrepreneurs, and foundations where each of these entities work cohesively and collaboratively to foster pioneering research initiatives, student projects, scholarships for deserving students, technology development and deployment and the infrastructural development at the Institute.

heading: Inauguration Ceremony of the Renovated Ganga, Jamuna & Godavari Ho
plain_text: ## Inauguration Ceremony of the Renovated Ganga, Jamuna & Godavari Hostels The inauguration ceremony of the Renovated Ganga, Jamuna & Godavari hostels took place on April 5, 2024 , at the IIT Madras campus. heading: Social Impact Club 2024-Chennai Edition
plain_text: ## Social Impact Club 2024-Chennai Edition The Social Impact Club 2024-Chennai Edition was held on August 3, 2024 , at Chennai, bringing together senior CSR leaders from over a dozen organizations to discuss the crucial topic of establishing reliable metrics and assessment frameworks for measuring CSR impact . heading: Social Impact Club 2024-Delhi Edition
plain_text: ## Social Impact Club 2024-Delhi Edition The Social Impact Club 2024-Delhi Edition , was held on October 1, 2024 , in New Delhi on the theme 'Transforming Healthcare through Technology.' heading: IIT Madras CSR Summit & Awards 2024
plain_text: ## IIT Madras CSR Summit & Awards 2024 The IIT Madras CSR Summit & Awards 2024 was held on December 13, 2024 , at the Student Activity Centre (SAC) in the IIT Madras. The event, themed 'Viksit Bharat 2047: Driving Inclusive Growth through CSR & Technology,' brought together over 200 corporate leaders, CSR heads, and public sector representatives to explore the intersection of technology and social impact. The event was graced by Dr. TRB Rajaa , T amil Nadu's Minister for Industries, in the presence of Prof. V Kamakoti, Director of IIT Madras. The summit featured panel discussions, showcases, and networking sessions, alongside the presentation of the 'Viksit Bharat 2047-IIT Madras Innovative Tech-for-Tomorrow CSR Awards.' Notable awards included Herbalife India, for its AquaEco digital aquaculture project, and CNH Industrial for its sustainable crop stubble burning reduction initiative. This summit highlighted IIT Madras' leadership in fostering industry-academia collaboration and promoting technology-driven CSR aligned with India's vision for inclusive growth by 2047. <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image --> <!-- image -->

## Subra Suresh Distinguished Lecture-Dr. Yann LeCun The Subra Suresh Distinguished Lecture by Dr. Yann LeCun, Turing Award winner and Chief AI Scientist at Meta, was held on October 22, 2024, at The Music Academy, Chennai. Organized by IIT Madras, the lecture focused on 'How Could Machines Reach Human-Level Intelligence?', where Dr. LeCun introduced advanced cognitive architectures in AI, including Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA). Supported by Mr. Gopalakrishnan's generous contribution, the lecture reflected IIT Madras' commitment to hosting global leaders in science and technology. <!-- image --> <!-- image -->

heading: 7.2.1.1.4. Joint Doctoral Programme
plain_text: ## 7.2.1.1.4. Joint Doctoral Programme The Joint Doctoral Programme (JDP) at IITM offers PhD scholars a unique opportunity to enhance their thesis work through substantial research exposure and collaboration with 19 prestigious partner institutes and universities worldwide. Under this programme, scholars can conduct research for 12 to 18 months with a host faculty member at one of the partner institutes. In the academic year 2024-25, we enrolled two inbound students from the University of Melbourne and École centrale de Nantes (ECN), including one student from Azerbaijan. 16 scholars across various disciplines completed their joint PhD programmes, with host institutes across Singapore, Australia, Germany, France, and the USA.

heading: JFBMP Partner Universities
plain_text: ## JFBMP Partner Universities Since 2022, the Jointly Funded Bilateral Mobility Program (JFBMP) has partnered with several prestigious universities across the globe, beginning with University College London in 2022. In 2023, new collaborations were established with the University of Sydney, Tel Aviv University, National Tsing Hua University (NTHU) (Taiwan), Deakin University, King's College London, and the University of Exeter-all in the first round of that year. In 2024, partnerships continued to grow with the University of Hull, Tel Aviv University (for a second round), and the University of Sydney (second round). heading: 7.2.3.4.1. About IITM Zanzibar
plain_text: ## 7.2.3.4.1. About IITM Zanzibar IIT Madras Zanzibar (IITMZ), established in 2023, is the first international campus of IIT Madras. The inception of this new campus in Zanzibar, Tanzania, marks a significant step in strengthening the ties between India and Africa. IITM Zanzibar promises to bring the same rigour that has defined IIT Madras' academic culture to its Zanzibar campus to contribute substantively to the region's human resources development. Currently, IITMZ offers one undergraduate programme and two Master of Technology programmes as full-time degree programmes, as well as one Web-enabled MTech programme, and the programmes are expected to grow. The student cohort comprises a diverse group, with excellent representation from India, Zanzibar, Tanzania, Nepal, Bangladesh, Zambia, and Kenya, nearly 40% of whom are women.

heading: Accelerating Net Zero 2.0, the Energy Consortium
plain_text: ## Accelerating Net Zero 2.0, the Energy Consortium In continuation with the first, the second issue of Accelerating Net Zero was published in February 2025 as part of World Energy Day. In the second edition of a short series of white papers, we brought together four seminal topics and what it takes to achieve net zero. - Startups: Cultivating a vibrant startup ecosystem to accelerate the commercialisation and scale-up of groundbreaking ideas - Academic Programmes: Offering globally recognized programmes, including online courses and training programmes, to a global audience - Research & Consultancy: Pioneering cutting-edge research and providing expert consultancy services in critical and emerging technology areas such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, sustainable technologies, quantum computing, cybersecurity, space tech, green tech, etc. - IP & Technology Transfer: Commercialising intellectual property (IP) to spur economic growth and development This year (2024-25) marked a transformative leap in IIT Madras' mission to internationalise innovation, research, the startup ecosystem, and academic programmes for enhancing employability and fostering entrepreneurship, ensuring that IITM's legacy of excellence reaches every corner of the globe. Through strategic outreach across the UAE, USA, Germany, Malaysia, and beyond, IITM Global is shaping a truly international future for India's deep tech landscape.

heading: 8.3.3. One Nation One Subscription (ONOS)
plain_text: ## 8.3.3. One Nation One Subscription (ONOS) In response to the vision of making India Atmanirbhar and Viksit Bharat @ 2047, the Government of India (GOI) approved the One Nation One Subscription (ONOS) scheme through a national subscription coordinated by the Information and Library Network (INFLIBNET) Centre to provide country-wide access to international high-impact scholarly research articles and journal publications. ONOS intends to acquire national licenses for e-journal/database subscriptions from prominent journal publishers. A total of 30 major international publishers have been included in ONOS. All the journals published by these publishers will be accessible to the participating institutions' students, faculty members and researchers starting its operation from 1st January 2025. Before ONOS, access to subscription journals was acquired through the e-ShodhSindhu Consortium for Higher Education Electronic Resources, which is now merged into ONOS. The main objective of e-ShodhSindhu was to provide access to qualitative electronic resources, including full-text, bibliographic and factual databases, at lower subscription rates to universities, colleges, and centrally funded technical institutions in India. IIT Madras had access to 15 e-resources from e-ShodhSindhu for 2023-24.

Heading: 8.3.3. One Nation One Subscription (ONOS)

Content:
## 8.3.3. One Nation One Subscription (ONOS) In response to the vision of making India Atmanirbhar and Viksit Bharat @ 2047, the Government of India (GOI) approved the One Nation One Subscription (ONOS) scheme through a national subscription coordinated by the Information and Library Network (INFLIBNET) Centre to provide country-wide access to international high-impact scholarly research articles and journal publications. ONOS intends to acquire national licenses for e-journal/database subscriptions from prominent journal publishers. A total of 30 major international publishers have been included in ONOS. All the journals published by these publishers will be accessible to the participating institutions' students, faculty members and researchers starting its operation from 1st January 2025. Before ONOS, access to subscription journals was acquired through the e-ShodhSindhu Consortium for Higher Education Electronic Resources, which is now merged into ONOS. The main objective of e-ShodhSindhu was to provide access to qualitative electronic resources, including full-text, bibliographic and factual databases, at lower subscription rates to universities, colleges, and centrally funded technical institutions in India. IIT Madras had access to 15 e-resources from e-ShodhSindhu for 2023-24.

heading: 9.1. Hostels
plain_text: ## 9.1. Hostels Most of the students reside in hostels on campus. Currently, there are 16 men's and 5 women's hostels for undergraduate and postgraduate students and research scholars. A total of 10,000+ seats are available to accommodate 10,800+ students (2600+ female and 8200+ male students). There are 11 dining halls that cater to hostel residents and a few day scholars. Ten of these dining halls are located in three mess complexes-five in Himalaya, three in Nilgiri, two in Vindhyaand one is in Cauvery hostel. All the dining halls are run by private caterers. Students decide the mess menu with the help of a nutritionist and culinary specialists. The caterer and rate are selected through a tender process. A couple of mess menus are of à la carte type served in the food court. Dining facility registrations and mess allocation to students are done online. The Mess Monitoring and Control Committee (MMCC) ensures the hygiene and quality of the food served and also supervises the tendering process. The housekeeping services in the hostels are outsourced. Each hostel is administered by Students' Amenities and Activities 9. Chapter 9 a Warden (a faculty member), Assistant Warden(s) (a research fellow or project staff), and a Hostel Council consisting of student secretaries. Each hostel office is supported by the Office of Hostel Management (OHM) staff, which is a centrally administered body and looks after the overall functioning of the hostels. The OHM takes care of online mess registration, mess accounts, biometric entry to hostels/dining facilities, temporary guest accommodation, online processes associated with vacating student rooms, students' (including day scholars' and married research scholars' families) and staff members' medical insurance, online bulk accommodation facilities for conferences, short-term courses and other events, and student festivals' ticketing and merchandise. There are 100+ employees (permanent + contract) on the roll at the OHM. Details on the Council of Wardens, Chairperson, Vice Chairperson and Hostel Management are available on the website: ccw.iitm.ac.in.

heading: 9.5.2. Content Highlights
plain_text: ## 9.5.2. Content Highlights Academics and Student Life: T5E published valuable content to aid student knowledge, including articles detailing the latest academic reforms, a comprehensive guide to the role of a teaching assistant, global research internship experiences, and semester-exchange journeys. Reports and interviews on the recently established Departments of Data Science and AI, and Medical Sciences and Technology were conducted. Interviews were held with the Inter-IIT Tech Guild leaders on their preparation, and the IIT-Madras Aquatics Team on their experiences at the Inter-IIT Aquatics Meet. Several other pieces capturing diverse aspects of campus life were published, including articles on birding at IIT Madras, campus fashion, the Institute lingo, and an internship season guide, among others. Opinion: In-depth opinion pieces examined key policy developments, including the introduction of the Sports Excellence Admissions and the Fine Arts and Cultural Excellence (FACE) programmes, presenting the viewpoints of various stakeholders involved. Various satirical and lighthearted pieces provided commentary on significant campus issues, ranging from academic policies to internship drive experiences. Student Governance: This year saw the launch of new initiatives aimed at deepening T5E's coverage of student governance in order to foster transparency and informed engagement within the General Student Body (GSB). In addition to 18 closed-door interviews with Executive Council candidates, there was a detailed coverage of 8 SLC sessions occurring throughout the year, and a report on the December Parliament trip: - T5E conducted its first Executive Council roundtable, where outgoing Executive Council secretaries participated in a moderated discussion to share their reflections and learnings from their terms in office. - A media briefing was held with the representatives of various IITs at the Pan IIT Student Governance Summit hosted by IIT Madras in October 2024, gathering reflections on their governance structures and best practices.

heading: 9.7. International & Alumni Relations (I&AR) Secretary
plain_text: ## 9.7. International & Alumni Relations (I&AR) Secretary The functioning of the I&AR student council for 2024-25 had three legs-improving alumni and student engagement, increasing & improving the brand of IIT Madras' student culture, and enhancing the brand of IIT Madras as a global institute of eminence. Recall was a novel initiative executed by the I&AR student council this year envisioning to connect the young alumni to the students applying for jobs or higher education by inviting them back to the Institute. Through Recall we also envisioned to bridge the disconnect between the first reunion after 5 years for alumni and helping them keep in touch with the Institute via the anchor of placements and placements in collaboration with the office of Alumni & Corporate Relations (A&CR). Following the attempt to keep the young alumni connected to the Institute, we also started a mentorship programme for final year students sitting for placements by mapping students from graduating batch to a group of students interested in a niche like product management, software engineering etc. We had a cohort of approximately 150 student mentors who were each mapped to a group of 3 students with the help of the Placement team. Additionally, to improve participation of PG alumni in reunions and their connect with the Institute, we organised PG reunions with AIRSS in collaboration with the A&CR office Finally, the I&AR student council also successfully organised its legacy events like Reunions, Parents' Day, AlumNite and Willkommen with the A&CR office and IITMAA and curated 3000+ yearbooks for the graduating batch. On the branding front, IITM Television released several reels and videos showcasing the vibrant student culture at IIT Madras. We also started a new initiative called 'Discover Chennai' envisioning to brand and educate about the rich culture of arts, education, food etc. in Chennai to students who are aspiring to join IIT Madras. In collaboration with the Heritage Centre, we organised several 'Heritage Hunts' to help educate the students about our rich heritage of student culture fostered over 60+ years of IIT Madras. We also invited and hosted several alumni from different parts of the history of IIT Madras to share and document their experiences during their student life at IIT Madras and share their insights from their journeys in life so far with the students through articles and video interviews. In collaboration with the African Students' Association and the Office of Global Engagement, the I&AR student council organised several events and sessions to acculturate the international students with our culture and educate our students about theirs. We also led the inception of the first ever community of international alumni and connected them to the current international students to facilitate transfer of knowledge and experience. We also started several initiatives in collaboration with the Office of Global Engagement to brand our international alumni and students and highlight the impact IIT Madras is making in their lives with respect to the exposure and opportunities and showcasing the budding international community at IIT Madras with International Day.

heading: 9.9.1. Shaastra 2025: Fractal Frontiers
plain_text: ## 9.9.1. Shaastra 2025: Fractal Frontiers Shaastra 2025, themed 'Fractal Frontiers,' lit up the campus from January 3-7, 2025, setting new benchmarks for innovation and engagement. For the first time in its history, the Institute Open House was conducted concurrently with Shaastra on January 3-4, attracting an unprecedented 60,000 registrations from across the Nation. The participation demonstrated remarkable diversity, drawing school students, academics, and working professionals alike. The Open House showcased IIT Madras' pioneering research through 80 meticulously curated stalls, over 90 laboratories, and 15 Centres of Excellence, offering visitors a comprehensive glimpse into the Institute's groundbreaking work. Intellectual discourse flourished with lectures from luminaries such as Dr. Sujatha Ramadorai, Prof. Subir Sachdev, Mr. Nambi Narayanan, and Dr. Harsh Gupta, who shared insights that expanded the frontiers of knowledge. Shaastra's social conscience was evident in 'Uzhavu,' a campaign that underscored our commitment to agricultural sustainability. The flagship Future Cities Summit and IndustriAI conference on smart manufacturing demonstrated our foresight in addressing pressing challenges. 'Rewire,' Shaastra's innovative initiative focused on cognitive enhancement, achieved remarkable success. The cultural dimension was enriched by captivating performances from Gurleen Pannu and Karan Kanchan, creating a holistic experience that celebrated both intellect and artistry. <!-- image --> <!-- image -->

heading: 9.12. Inclusive Education
plain_text: ## 9.12. Inclusive Education Inclusive Education of Students with Special Needs, IIT Madras, seeks to nurture students with disabilities (SwDs) so that they become professionally competent and personally independent, by enabling reasonable participation in - Team Pragati connected 2000+ students for Union Public Service Commission Civil Services Examination (UPSC CSE) and Common Admission Test (CAT) preparation - Conducted IViL (IIT for Villages) visits exposing students to rural India challenges - Launched Nivarak Portal with Buy & Sell platform and the Institute chatbot for query resolution. - Organised cultural events including Mehkaar-E-Mohabbat (poetry & qawwali) and Ethnic Day 'Roots and Rhythm' curricular, co-curricular and extra-curricular activities in the IIT campus. IIT Madras provides assistive technologies to help them to learn and also ensures safe and comfortable living conditions on the campus. Prof. V Kamakoti, Director, IIT Madras inaugurated the Inclusive Education Resource Centre (IERC) on November 6, 2024 at Central Library. The Centre offers different assistive technology devices for students with low vision or blindness and other disabilities. The devices such as Kibo XS, Dolphin Supernova magnifier, Supernova screen reader and magnifier, Ruby 7' high definition (HD) video magnifier, Ruby 10' HD video magnifier, Mouse magnifier, talking calculator, tactile geometry kit, hands-free magnifier, rechargeable LED (light emitting diode), eyeglasses bracket/magnifier, etc. are available here. The Centre is easily accessible (facilities like ramp, lift, disabled friendly washroom, drinking water, etc.) and convenient for students to use. In the Centre, the amenities are arranged, like height adjustable tables, large screen desktops, switch boards etc., to an accessible height. The Centre is open from 9:00 AM to 12:00 AM midnight which enables them to use the devices extensively. To address the mobility issues of students with locomotor challenges, the Office of the Dean (Students) provides e-carts, e-bikes, wheelchairs or e-cycles depending upon the opinion of the medical team. All the hostels are equipped with ramps, lifts, and rooms in the ground floor with attached washroom facility as per their requirement. In certain cases where the student needs help to do daily living chores, the parent or caretaker is allowed to stay with them. White cane training would be provided for those with vision impairment. The parking spots are well defined, sign boards are well placed and tactile paving has been done in some of the classrooms. Ramps and lifts are available in all buildings. To address pain and maintain good body posture, the IERC refers the students to physicians or physiotherapists. In mess and hostels, comfortable seating arrangements are provided on need basis. Those who have visual impairment will be referred for ophthalmologic consultation and based on the test results will be provided with spectacles, magnifiers, or any relevant medical procedures as per their needs. Those who have hearing impairment also get similar support. They will get a hearing evaluation done and based on that hearing devices will either be tuned or procured. Some faculties would use Multi Mic with Bluetooth connection so that students can hear the voice clearly. The faculties would share slides/PowerPoint

heading: 9.12.1. Training Programmes Attended
plain_text: ## 9.12.1. Training Programmes Attended The IE team attended the following programmes- - Idea Lab 4: 'Making Faculty Agents of Inclusive Teaching in Classrooms' group-a focused group discussion organised by Ashoka University - The online and offline meetings of Capacity Building Programme on Specific Learning Disabilities under Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Programme (MMTTP) - Meeting with the Office of Accessible Education, IIT Delhi to discuss about the IE activities of IIT Madras. - SwDs attended Sports4all-Thiramai (basketball) - SwDs performed in Avaa Dingi -a musical and cultural event <!-- image --> presentations (PPTs)/lecture notes etc. so that students can learn the subjects easily. In addition to all these, volunteer services (both inside and outside classroom) for taking class notes, doubt clarification, lab work, assignment submission, etc. are being provided. Scribes, large font size question papers, extra time for the exams, extra time for assignment submission, etc. also permitted. Conversion of textbooks to accessible content is also being done for visually challenged students. Financial assistance is provided to help to get laptop, academic fees, and to procure other devices such as callipers. Scholarship related issues, or other relevant support is also offered. Training sessions were conducted for students to learn various assistive devices such as Kibo XS and AI based technologies. Sensitisation trainings are organised every year for new faculties to learn about disability. The IERC also organised 2 online training programmes for course instructors to create awareness about disabilities and how to empower students with disabilities to excel in academics. The Inclusive Education (IE) team interacts with different stakeholders such as TTK Centre for Rehabilitation Research and Device Development, National Centre for Assistive Health Technologies, IIT Madras (NCAHT-IITM), and Enability Foundation for Rehabilitation. The team also takes part in Assistive Technology Conference: EMPOWER in order to stay updated about the field. The Institute also encouraged the staff to attend the online and offline meetings of Capacity Building Programme on Specific Learning Disabilities under Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Programme (MMTTP). The IERC also regularly organised programmes for students on different topics like a talk by a medical doctor Dr. Gowrishankar from Institute Hospital about maintaining good health, an art therapy session and a question & answer (Q&A) session by an alumnus for placement. The students were also encouraged to participate in various sports (like for Sports4all or Thiramai) event or cultural events like Avaa Dingi.

In addition to all these, volunteer services (both inside and outside classroom) for taking class notes, doubt clarification, lab work, assignment submission, etc. are being provided. Scribes, large font size question papers, extra time for the exams, extra time for assignment submission, etc. also permitted. Conversion of textbooks to accessible content is also being done for visually challenged students. Financial assistance is provided to help to get laptop, academic fees, and to procure other devices such as callipers. Scholarship related issues, or other relevant support is also offered. Training sessions were conducted for students to learn various assistive devices such as Kibo XS and AI based technologies. Sensitisation trainings are organised every year for new faculties to learn about disability. The IERC also organised 2 online training programmes for course instructors to create awareness about disabilities and how to empower students with disabilities to excel in academics. The Inclusive Education (IE) team interacts with different stakeholders such as TTK Centre for Rehabilitation Research and Device Development, National Centre for Assistive Health Technologies, IIT Madras (NCAHT-IITM), and Enability Foundation for Rehabilitation. The team also takes part in Assistive Technology Conference: EMPOWER in order to stay updated about the field. The Institute also encouraged the staff to attend the online and offline meetings of Capacity Building Programme on Specific Learning Disabilities under Malaviya Mission Teacher Training Programme (MMTTP). The IERC also regularly organised programmes for students on different topics like a talk by a medical doctor Dr. Gowrishankar from Institute Hospital about maintaining good health, an art therapy session and a question & answer (Q&A) session by an alumnus for placement. The students were also encouraged to participate in various sports (like for Sports4all or Thiramai) event or cultural events like Avaa Dingi.

heading: 9.13. Gymkhana Office
plain_text: ## 9.13. Gymkhana Office The Institute Gymkhana takes care of the general welfare of the students and their activities. Sports activities form an integral part of the overall development of personality, which prepares the students to overcome challenges in their life after graduation. The following tournaments were attended and conducted during the year 2024-25 under the guidance of the Institute Gymkhana of IIT Madras- - Sports Fest 2024 - 37th Inter-IIT Aquatics Meet - 57th Inter-IIT Sports Meet - All India Inter-Collegiate Volleyball Tournament-Jimmy George Cup - All India Inter-Collegiate Basketball Tournament-Gerhard Fischer (GF) & Kokila Rajaiah (KR) - Chennai Inter-Collegiate Tournament - Inter-Hostel Championship- Schroeter Cup - Dean's Trophy Tournament-Inter-Hostel - National Sports Organisation (NSO) selections for 1st year BTech/Dual Degree students - Clubs - Recreational Course - Inter-University Team Selection (Beach Volleyball) We started off with the PG Summer League, which set the tone for the rest of the year. Soon after, we launched Sportify, a freshers' immersion programme that gave the incoming 2025 batch the chance to explore and try out all our sporting facilities. Over 500 students participated, and it was incredible to see so much excitement right from the start. Throughout the year, the Sports Organising Committee worked hard to keep everyone engaged with activities like the 5K Marathon, Wellness Run, beginner sessions, match screenings, and more. In September, we successfully hosted our inter-collegiate sports fest, where our athletes performed brilliantly and secured several medals. In October, our aquatics team competed in the 38th InterIIT Aquatics Meet at IIT Indore. Our women's team finished as runners-up, and our water polo team brought home the bronze-a proud moment for all of us. Later, at the 57th Inter-IIT Sports Meet held across IIT Indore and IIT Kanpur, our entire contingent put in a tremendous effort- - We were crowned Women's Overall General Champions for the second consecutive year - We finished 2nd overall in the General Championship - And the men's team secured 4th place Our medal tally was strong- - 1 Gold: Table tennis (men) - 6 Silver: Aquatics (women), badminton (women), basketball (women), tennis (men & women), table tennis (women) - 6 Bronze: Athletics (men & women), squash (women), volleyball (men), water polo, and weightlifting - 4th Place in chess In March, we also hosted the All India Jimmy George Volleyball and GF & KR Basketball Tournaments, where both our men's and women's teams competed with full spirit. Our Dean's Trophy and Schroeter events continued to bring out the competitive energy and house pride in every participant.

heading: 5. English Research Project
plain_text: ## 5. English Research Project - A research project based on the aptitude of rural girl students in English communication, was taken up by IViL in collaboration with NSS, under the guidance of Professor Rajesh Kumar (Head of Department, Humanities and Social Sciences). - The project began with a baseline test across four schools in Chengalpettu and Thiruvallur, revealing widespread issues in grammar, spelling, and sentence structure, alongside low confidence in using English. - Two schools-Government Girls School, Madharpakkam, and Panchayat Union Middle School, Thirusulam-were selected for intervention with 20 IITM volunteers conducting sessions bi-weekly in July. <!-- image -->

heading: 12.1. BTech & Dual Degree Programme
plain_text: ## 12.1. BTech & Dual Degree Programme As per the Government of India (GOI) orders, 27%, 15% and 7.5% of the total seats are reserved for students belonging to the Other Backward Classes (OBC), Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST) respectively in the BTech & Dual Degree programme. These students are admitted through the Joint Entrance Examination (Advanced) with a relaxation. These students have to get only 60% of the marks obtained by the last student of the General category to get qualified for admission. During counselling prior to admission, an advisor will explain to each student the requirements of different branches. This helps the students to choose a suitable branch based upon their capability and interest.

heading: 13.3.1. Organic Landscaping and Lawn Maintenance
plain_text: ## 13.3.1. Organic Landscaping and Lawn Maintenance The Horticulture Unit, functioning under the Engineering Unit (EU), maintains 66,181 square metres of lawn, which includes: a) 42,838 sqm at various locations across the campus b) 23,343 sqm of turf in stadium and playfields All maintenance activities strictly follow sustainable and organic practices. The use of chemical pesticides is completely prohibited. Only neem-based Azadirachtin (10,000 ppm) is selectively applied when pest populations cross the Economic Threshold Level (ETL). Vermicompost, generated from organic waste (primarily from hostel messes), is used as the sole nutritional supplement for lawns and gardens. The lawn turf at the hockey ground has been organically developed using local grass species. These green patches not only enhance aesthetics but also serve as feeding grounds for cervid species such as blackbuck and spotted deer. <!-- image --> <!-- image -->

heading: 13.3.2. Habitat Enrichment for Wildlife
plain_text: ## 13.3.2. Habitat Enrichment for Wildlife To expand grazing areas for the Chital and Blackbuck, native grass species like CO4 are being planted as mother plants near the Stadium. These grasses will be propagated using ratooning methods and used as fodder for wild herbivores. The Horticulture Section also maintains water troughs at 90 locations across the campus for the Institute's cervid population. These containers are cleaned and refilled daily, and also support other fauna including bonnet macaques, squirrels, and various bird species during summer.

heading: 13.4. Public Health
plain_text: ## 13.4. Public Health The horticulture section takes care of mosquito-breeding grounds and control of larval and adult mosquitoes by spraying larvicide and fumigation. It also takes care of termite control in the campus. Solid waste management is being carried out as per Tamil Nadu Solid Waste Management Rules 2016. Wastes are getting source segregated, collected door-to-door, and recycled/disposed after secondary segregation. Bio-medical waste and e-waste are getting disposed through a TNPCB-authorized agency. Hazardous waste generated inside the campus is being safely disposed through a TNCPB-approved agency (Re-Sustainability).

heading: 13.5. Telephone Facilities
plain_text: ## 13.5. Telephone Facilities PBX telephone system: The campus telephone facility has been extended to the office and residential quarters of faculty members, laboratories of various departments, and miscellaneous services from HiPath 4000 ISDN PBX system with 5000-line capacity interfaced with BSNL through ISDN PRA lines. There are 18 remote telephone systems housed at various buildings in Academic, Hostel, and Residential Zones connected to the main PBX system via optical fiber link. By using BSNL point-to-point 1GBPS Internet Leased Line, both voice and data have been extended to IITM Discovery Campus at Thaiyur since a new telephone exchange has been installed at Thaiyur Campus. The complaints of campus telephone lines are attended within two hours from the time of receipt/ registration. Online campus telephone directory is available on the institute website under the 'Directory' tab: iitm.ac.in/ directory

As a part of the support service, the section functions 24×7 for the security requirements, various types of emergencies and contingencies, which may adversely affect the normal life of the campus. As per the security policy of IIT Madras, core security functions and areas are being be manned by the IIT's own security personnel and allied security functions and areas are looked after by the outsourced security agencies and coordinated by the Institute personnel. The Institute has also been progressively introducing greater automation. The current year has been eventful and has been very rewarding too.
